module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.DirectLimit
public import Mathlib.Order.DirectedInverseSystem

/-!
# Actual mixed-stage maps for the tensor/direct-limit diagonal

These maps use the existing native module direct limit and tensor maps.
Changing the common upper stage does not change the represented tensor.
No transition injectivity or flatness is assumed.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

open scoped TensorProduct

universe r i m n

namespace TensorProduct

variable {R : Type r} [CommSemiring R] {ι : Type i} [Preorder ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {M : ι → Type m} [∀ j, AddCommMonoid (M j)] [∀ j, Module R (M j)]
  {N : ι → Type n} [∀ j, AddCommMonoid (N j)] [∀ j, Module R (N j)]
  (f : ∀ a b, a ≤ b → M a →ₗ[R] M b)
  (g : ∀ a b, a ≤ b → N a →ₗ[R] N b)

/-- The simultaneous transition is the actual native tensor map. -/
def diagonalTransition (a b : ι) (h : a ≤ b) :
    M a ⊗[R] N a →ₗ[R] M b ⊗[R] N b :=
  TensorProduct.map (f a b h) (g a b h)

/-- The native module direct limit of simultaneous tensor stages. -/
abbrev diagonalLimit :=
  Module.DirectLimit (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j) (diagonalTransition f g)

/-- Push a mixed-stage tensor to an actual common upper stage and take its
native module-colimit class. -/
def diagonalStageAt (a b c : ι) (ha : a ≤ c) (hb : b ≤ c) :
    M a ⊗[R] N b →ₗ[R] diagonalLimit f g :=
  (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
    (diagonalTransition f g) c).comp (TensorProduct.map (f a c ha) (g b c hb))

@[simp]
theorem diagonalStageAt_tmul (a b c : ι) (ha : a ≤ c) (hb : b ≤ c)
    (x : M a) (y : N b) :
    diagonalStageAt f g a b c ha hb (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) =
      Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
        (diagonalTransition f g) c (f a c ha x ⊗ₜ[R] g b c hb y) := by
  simp only [diagonalStageAt, LinearMap.comp_apply, TensorProduct.map_tmul]

variable [DirectedSystem M (f · · ·)] [DirectedSystem N (g · · ·)]

omit [DecidableEq ι] in
/-- The actual simultaneous tensor transitions form a directed system.
Only the original preorder and factor-system laws are needed. -/
instance diagonalDirectedSystem :
    DirectedSystem (fun a => M a ⊗[R] N a) (diagonalTransition f g · · ·) where
  map_self a z := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul x y =>
        simp only [diagonalTransition, TensorProduct.map_tmul,
          DirectedSystem.map_self' f, DirectedSystem.map_self' g]
    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
  map_map {c b a} hab hbc z := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul x y =>
        simp only [diagonalTransition, TensorProduct.map_tmul,
          DirectedSystem.map_map' f hab hbc, DirectedSystem.map_map' g hab hbc]
    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]

/-- Raising the common upper stage gives the same actual class. -/
theorem diagonalStageAt_mono (a b c d : ι) (ha : a ≤ c) (hb : b ≤ c)
    (h : c ≤ d) :
    diagonalStageAt f g a b c ha hb =
      diagonalStageAt f g a b d (ha.trans h) (hb.trans h) := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro x y
  rw [diagonalStageAt_tmul, diagonalStageAt_tmul]
  have he := Module.DirectLimit.of_f
    (R := R) (ι := ι) (G := fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
    (f := diagonalTransition f g) (i := c) (j := d) (hij := h)
    (x := f a c ha x ⊗ₜ[R] g b c hb y)
  simp only [diagonalTransition, TensorProduct.map_tmul,
    DirectedSystem.map_map' f, DirectedSystem.map_map' g] at he
  exact he.symm

variable [IsDirectedOrder ι]

/-- Independence of the chosen upper stage follows from an actual further
common upper stage and directed-system composition. -/
theorem diagonalStageAt_eq (a b c d : ι) (ha : a ≤ c) (hb : b ≤ c)
    (ha' : a ≤ d) (hb' : b ≤ d) :
    diagonalStageAt f g a b c ha hb = diagonalStageAt f g a b d ha' hb' := by
  obtain ⟨e, hc, hd⟩ := exists_ge_ge c d
  exact (diagonalStageAt_mono f g a b c e ha hb hc).trans
    (diagonalStageAt_mono f g a b d e ha' hb' hd).symm


/-- The canonical mixed-stage map uses an actual common upper stage. Its value
is independent of that choice by diagonalStageAt_eq. -/
def diagonalStage (a b : ι) : M a ⊗[R] N b →ₗ[R] diagonalLimit f g :=
  let h := exists_ge_ge a b
  diagonalStageAt f g a b (Classical.choose h)
    (Classical.choose_spec h).1 (Classical.choose_spec h).2

theorem diagonalStage_eq (a b c : ι) (ha : a ≤ c) (hb : b ≤ c) :
    diagonalStage f g a b = diagonalStageAt f g a b c ha hb := by
  let h := exists_ge_ge a b
  exact diagonalStageAt_eq f g a b (Classical.choose h) c
    (Classical.choose_spec h).1 (Classical.choose_spec h).2 ha hb

/-- Compatibility with the actual transition in the second tensor factor. -/
theorem diagonalStage_comp_right (a b c : ι) (h : b ≤ c) :
    (diagonalStage f g a c).comp
        (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : M a →ₗ[R] M a) (g b c h)) =
      diagonalStage f g a b := by
  obtain ⟨d, ha, hc⟩ := exists_ge_ge a c
  rw [diagonalStage_eq f g a c d ha hc, diagonalStage_eq f g a b d ha (h.trans hc)]
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro x y
  simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, TensorProduct.map_tmul, LinearMap.id_apply,
    diagonalStageAt_tmul, DirectedSystem.map_map' g]

/-- Compatibility with the actual transition in the first tensor factor. -/
theorem diagonalStage_comp_left (a b c : ι) (h : a ≤ c) :
    (diagonalStage f g c b).comp
        (TensorProduct.map (f a c h) (LinearMap.id : N b →ₗ[R] N b)) =
      diagonalStage f g a b := by
  obtain ⟨d, hc, hb⟩ := exists_ge_ge c b
  rw [diagonalStage_eq f g c b d hc hb, diagonalStage_eq f g a b d (h.trans hc) hb]
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro x y
  simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, TensorProduct.map_tmul, LinearMap.id_apply,
    diagonalStageAt_tmul, DirectedSystem.map_map' f]

/-- At an actual diagonal stage the canonical mixed-stage map is the native
stage injection, rather than a caller-supplied inverse formula. -/
theorem diagonalStage_self (a : ι) :
    diagonalStage f g a a =
      Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j) (diagonalTransition f g) a := by
  rw [diagonalStage_eq f g a a a le_rfl le_rfl]
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro x y
  simp only [diagonalStageAt_tmul, DirectedSystem.map_self' f, DirectedSystem.map_self' g]


omit [IsDirectedOrder ι] [DirectedSystem M (f · · ·)]
  [DirectedSystem N (g · · ·)] in
/-- The actual forward diagonal comparison is the native module-colimit lift
of the simultaneous stage injections into the two factor colimits. -/
def diagonalToTensor :
    diagonalLimit f g →ₗ[R] Module.DirectLimit M f ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g :=
  Module.DirectLimit.lift R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j) (diagonalTransition f g)
    (fun j => TensorProduct.map (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f j)
      (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g j)) (by
      intro a b h z
      have he :
          (TensorProduct.map (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f b)
              (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b)).comp (diagonalTransition f g a b h) =
            TensorProduct.map (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a)
              (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g a) := by
        apply TensorProduct.ext'
        intro x y
        simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, diagonalTransition, TensorProduct.map_tmul,
          Module.DirectLimit.of_f]
      exact LinearMap.congr_fun he z)

omit [IsDirectedOrder ι] [DirectedSystem M (f · · ·)]
  [DirectedSystem N (g · · ·)] in
/-- The whole forward stage tensor uses the native factor injections.
This characteristic needs no directedness or directed-system laws. -/
@[simp]
theorem diagonalToTensor_of (a : ι) (z : M a ⊗[R] N a) :
    diagonalToTensor f g
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
          (diagonalTransition f g) a z) =
      TensorProduct.map (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a)
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g a) z := by
  simp only [diagonalToTensor, Module.DirectLimit.lift_of]

omit [IsDirectedOrder ι] [DirectedSystem M (f · · ·)]
  [DirectedSystem N (g · · ·)] in
theorem diagonalToTensor_of_tmul (a : ι) (x : M a) (y : N a) :
    diagonalToTensor f g
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
          (diagonalTransition f g) a (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)) =
      Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g a y := by
  rw [diagonalToTensor_of, TensorProduct.map_tmul]

/-- Native tensor/direct-limit commutation in the second factor followed by
the computed mixed-stage lift. -/
def diagonalSecond (a : ι) :
    M a ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g →ₗ[R] diagonalLimit f g :=
  (Module.DirectLimit.lift R ι (fun b => M a ⊗[R] N b)
    (fun b c h => LinearMap.lTensor (M a) (g b c h))
    (fun b => diagonalStage f g a b) (by
      intro b c h z
      exact LinearMap.congr_fun (diagonalStage_comp_right f g a b c h) z)).comp
    (TensorProduct.directLimitRight g (M a)).toLinearMap

@[simp]
theorem diagonalSecond_tmul_of (a b : ι) (x : M a) (y : N b) :
    diagonalSecond f g a (x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y) =
      diagonalStage f g a b (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) := by
  let p : Module.DirectLimit (fun b => M a ⊗[R] N b)
      (fun b c h => LinearMap.lTensor (M a) (g b c h)) →ₗ[R] diagonalLimit f g :=
    Module.DirectLimit.lift R ι (fun b => M a ⊗[R] N b)
      (fun b c h => LinearMap.lTensor (M a) (g b c h))
      (fun b => diagonalStage f g a b) (by
        intro b c h z
        exact LinearMap.congr_fun (diagonalStage_comp_right f g a b c h) z)
  change p (TensorProduct.directLimitRight g (M a)
    (x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y)) = _
  have he := TensorProduct.directLimitRight_tmul_of (f := g) (M := M a) (i := b) x y
  have hp : p (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun b => M a ⊗[R] N b)
      (fun b c h => LinearMap.lTensor (M a) (g b c h)) b (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)) =
      diagonalStage f g a b (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) := by
    exact Module.DirectLimit.lift_of (R := R) (ι := ι)
      (G := fun b => M a ⊗[R] N b)
      (f := fun b c h => LinearMap.lTensor (M a) (g b c h))
      (fun b => diagonalStage f g a b) (by
        intro b c h z
        exact LinearMap.congr_fun (diagonalStage_comp_right f g a b c h) z)
      (i := b) (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)
  exact (congrArg p he).trans hp

/-- The second-factor lift respects the actual first-factor transition. -/
theorem diagonalSecond_comp (a c : ι) (h : a ≤ c) :
    (diagonalSecond f g c).comp (LinearMap.rTensor (Module.DirectLimit N g) (f a c h)) =
      diagonalSecond f g a := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro x z
  have hx :
      TensorProduct.curry
          ((diagonalSecond f g c).comp
            (LinearMap.rTensor (Module.DirectLimit N g) (f a c h))) x =
        TensorProduct.curry (diagonalSecond f g a) x := by
    apply Module.DirectLimit.hom_ext (R := R) (ι := ι) (G := N) (f := g)
    intro b
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro y
    change diagonalSecond f g c
        (f a c h x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y) =
      diagonalSecond f g a (x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y)
    rw [diagonalSecond_tmul_of, diagonalSecond_tmul_of]
    exact LinearMap.congr_fun (diagonalStage_comp_left f g a b c h) (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)
  exact LinearMap.congr_fun hx z

/-- The inverse candidate uses native single-moving-factor equivalences and
module-colimit lifts, with both transition compatibilities already earned. -/
def tensorToDiagonal :
    Module.DirectLimit M f ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g →ₗ[R] diagonalLimit f g :=
  (Module.DirectLimit.lift R ι (fun a => M a ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g)
    (fun a c h => LinearMap.rTensor (Module.DirectLimit N g) (f a c h))
    (fun a => diagonalSecond f g a) (by
      intro a c h z
      exact LinearMap.congr_fun (diagonalSecond_comp f g a c h) z)).comp
    (TensorProduct.directLimitLeft f (Module.DirectLimit N g)).toLinearMap

/-- Its mixed-stage characteristic is the actual common-stage tensor class. -/
@[simp]
theorem tensorToDiagonal_of_tmul_of (a b : ι) (x : M a) (y : N b) :
    tensorToDiagonal f g
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y) =
      diagonalStage f g a b (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) := by
  let p : Module.DirectLimit (fun a => M a ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g)
      (fun a c h => LinearMap.rTensor (Module.DirectLimit N g) (f a c h)) →ₗ[R]
        diagonalLimit f g :=
    Module.DirectLimit.lift R ι (fun a => M a ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g)
      (fun a c h => LinearMap.rTensor (Module.DirectLimit N g) (f a c h))
      (fun a => diagonalSecond f g a) (by
        intro a c h z
        exact LinearMap.congr_fun (diagonalSecond_comp f g a c h) z)
  change p (TensorProduct.directLimitLeft f (Module.DirectLimit N g)
    (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y)) = _
  have he := TensorProduct.directLimitLeft_tmul_of (f := f)
    (M := Module.DirectLimit N g) (i := a) x (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y)
  have hp : p (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun a => M a ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g)
      (fun a c h => LinearMap.rTensor (Module.DirectLimit N g) (f a c h)) a
        (x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y)) =
      diagonalStage f g a b (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) := by
    simp only [p, Module.DirectLimit.lift_of, diagonalSecond_tmul_of]
  exact (congrArg p he).trans hp


/-- The computed forward map sends a mixed-stage tensor to its two native
factor classes, independently of the common upper stage. -/
theorem diagonalToTensor_diagonalStage (a b : ι) (x : M a) (y : N b) :
    diagonalToTensor f g (diagonalStage f g a b (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)) =
      Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y := by
  obtain ⟨c, ha, hb⟩ := exists_ge_ge a b
  rw [diagonalStage_eq f g a b c ha hb, diagonalStageAt_tmul,
    diagonalToTensor_of_tmul, Module.DirectLimit.of_f, Module.DirectLimit.of_f]

/-- The inverse candidate followed by the forward map is identity on the
actual factor-colimit tensor product. -/
theorem diagonalToTensor_comp_tensorToDiagonal :
    (diagonalToTensor f g).comp (tensorToDiagonal f g) = LinearMap.id := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro x y
  have he :
      TensorProduct.curry ((diagonalToTensor f g).comp (tensorToDiagonal f g)) =
        TensorProduct.curry
          (LinearMap.id : Module.DirectLimit M f ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g →ₗ[R]
            Module.DirectLimit M f ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g) := by
    apply Module.DirectLimit.hom_ext (R := R) (ι := ι) (G := M) (f := f)
    intro a
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro u
    apply Module.DirectLimit.hom_ext (R := R) (ι := ι) (G := N) (f := g)
    intro b
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro v
    change diagonalToTensor f g
        (tensorToDiagonal f g
          (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a u ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b v)) =
      Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a u ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b v
    rw [tensorToDiagonal_of_tmul_of, diagonalToTensor_diagonalStage]
  exact LinearMap.congr_fun (LinearMap.congr_fun he x) y

/-- The forward map followed by the inverse is identity on the actual
simultaneous-stage module quotient. -/
theorem tensorToDiagonal_comp_diagonalToTensor :
    (tensorToDiagonal f g).comp (diagonalToTensor f g) = LinearMap.id := by
  apply Module.DirectLimit.hom_ext (R := R) (ι := ι)
    (G := fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j) (f := diagonalTransition f g)
  intro a
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro x y
  change tensorToDiagonal f g
      (diagonalToTensor f g
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
          (diagonalTransition f g) a (x ⊗ₜ[R] y))) =
    Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
      (diagonalTransition f g) a (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)
  rw [diagonalToTensor_of_tmul, tensorToDiagonal_of_tmul_of, diagonalStage_self]

/-- The canonical unbundled diagonal tensor/direct-limit equivalence.
The index, scalar and both module worlds are independent; no transition
injectivity, flatness, field or supplied inverse is assumed. -/
def directLimitDiagonal :
    diagonalLimit f g ≃ₗ[R] Module.DirectLimit M f ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit N g :=
  LinearEquiv.ofLinearMap (diagonalToTensor f g) (tensorToDiagonal f g)
    (diagonalToTensor_comp_tensorToDiagonal f g)
    (tensorToDiagonal_comp_diagonalToTensor f g)

/-- The whole stage tensor maps by the exact native injections of its factors. -/
@[simp]
theorem directLimitDiagonal_of (a : ι) (z : M a ⊗[R] N a) :
    directLimitDiagonal f g
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
          (diagonalTransition f g) a z) =
      TensorProduct.map (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a)
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g a) z := by
  exact diagonalToTensor_of f g a z

/-- The forward characteristic retains exactly the native simultaneous stage map. -/
theorem directLimitDiagonal_of_tmul (a : ι) (x : M a) (y : N a) :
    directLimitDiagonal f g
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
          (diagonalTransition f g) a (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)) =
      Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g a y :=
  diagonalToTensor_of_tmul f g a x y

/-- The inverse characteristic is the computed class at any actual common stage. -/
@[simp]
theorem directLimitDiagonal_symm_of_tmul_of (a b : ι) (x : M a) (y : N b) :
    (directLimitDiagonal f g).symm
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a x ⊗ₜ[R] Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g b y) =
      diagonalStage f g a b (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) :=
  tensorToDiagonal_of_tmul_of f g a b x y

/-- A stage tensor whose two factor classes give zero is killed at an actual
common later stage. This uses only additive monoids over a commutative semiring;
the supplied stage removes any need for a nonempty-index assumption. -/
theorem exists_eq_zero_of_map_to_directLimit_diagonal_eq_zero
    {a : ι} (z : M a ⊗[R] N a)
    (hz : TensorProduct.map (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι M f a)
      (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι N g a) z = 0) :
    ∃ c : ι, ∃ h : a ≤ c,
      TensorProduct.map (f a c h) (g a c h) z = 0 := by
  have hcolimit :
      Module.DirectLimit.of R ι (fun j => M j ⊗[R] N j)
        (diagonalTransition f g) a z = 0 := by
    apply (directLimitDiagonal f g).injective
    rw [directLimitDiagonal_of, map_zero]
    exact hz
  exact Module.DirectLimit.of.zero_exact hcolimit

end TensorProduct

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.DirectLimit.Diagonal

/-!
# Eventual vanishing in directed tensor systems

If a tensor at one stage maps to zero after both factors are included in a
direct limit, then it is already zero after some common later transition.
The proof uses the earned simultaneous tensor/direct-limit equivalence and
the native eventual-zero theorem for the concrete directed limit.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

open Module Module.DirectLimit

namespace TensorProduct

variable {R ι : Type*} [CommRing R] [DecidableEq ι]
variable [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι]
variable {G : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] [∀ i, Module R (G i)]
variable (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[R] G j)
variable [DirectedSystem G (f · · ·)]

/-- A stagewise tensor which vanishes after both factors map to the direct
limit vanishes after one common enlargement. -/
theorem exists_eq_zero_of_map_to_directLimit_tensor_eq_zero
    {i : ι} (x : G i ⊗[R] G i)
    (hx : TensorProduct.map
      (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i)
      (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i) x = 0) :
    ∃ j : ι, ∃ hij : i ≤ j,
      TensorProduct.map (f i j hij) (f i j hij) x = 0 := by
  exact exists_eq_zero_of_map_to_directLimit_diagonal_eq_zero f f x hx

end TensorProduct

namespace Module.DirectLimit

variable {R ι : Type*} [CommRing R] [DecidableEq ι]
variable [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι]
variable {G : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] [∀ i, Module R (G i)]
variable (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[R] G j)
variable [DirectedSystem G (f · · ·)]

/-- A finite family from one stage which vanishes in a module direct limit
is killed simultaneously at one common later stage. -/
theorem of.zero_exact_finite_family
    {I : Type*} [Finite I] {i : ι} (x : I → G i)
    (hx : ∀ a, Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i (x a) = 0) :
    ∃ j : ι, ∃ hij : i ≤ j, ∀ a, f i j hij (x a) = 0 := by
  classical
  let _ : Fintype I := Fintype.ofFinite I
  have aux : ∀ s : Finset I,
      ∃ j : ι, ∃ hij : i ≤ j, ∀ a ∈ s, f i j hij (x a) = 0 := by
    intro s
    induction s using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty => exact ⟨i, le_rfl, by simp⟩
    | @insert a s ha ih =>
        obtain ⟨j, hij, hsj⟩ := ih
        let xaJ := f i j hij (x a)
        have hxaJ : Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f j xaJ = 0 := by
          change Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f j (f i j hij (x a)) = 0
          rw [Module.DirectLimit.of_f]
          exact hx a
        obtain ⟨k, hjk, hxaK⟩ := Module.DirectLimit.of.zero_exact hxaJ
        refine ⟨k, hij.trans hjk, ?_⟩
        intro b hb
        rcases Finset.mem_insert.mp hb with rfl | hbs
        · rw [← DirectedSystem.map_map' f hij hjk]
          exact hxaK
        · rw [← DirectedSystem.map_map' f hij hjk,
            hsj b hbs, map_zero]
  obtain ⟨j, hij, hzero⟩ := aux Finset.univ
  exact ⟨j, hij, fun a => hzero a (Finset.mem_univ a)⟩

end Module.DirectLimit

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Basic
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.TwoDirectedSystems

/-!
# Positive tensor powers of directed module systems

For a directed system `G i`, this file equips every positive left-associated
tensor power of `G i` with its induced directed system.  Its direct limit is
canonically equivalent to the corresponding tensor power of `lim G`.
Consequently, an element of any positive tensor power that vanishes after
mapping to the direct limit already vanishes at one finite stage.

The positive power indexed by `n` has `n + 1` factors.  This convention
matches the positive tensor powers used by the arbitrary-weight Kummer cup
construction. The successor comparison uses the generalized simultaneous
tensor/direct-limit equivalence directly, keeping this same positive-power
carrier and its canonical stage maps.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open Module Module.DirectLimit

namespace TensorProduct

universe u v w x y

variable {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} [CommRing R] [DecidableEq ι]
variable [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι]

/-- The left-associated tensor power with `n + 1` factors, bundled as an
`R`-module.  Bundling the recursion keeps the induced additive and module
structures canonical in every universe. -/
noncomputable def positiveTensorPowerModuleObj
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    ℕ → ModuleCat.{max u w} R
  | 0 => ModuleCat.of R (R ⊗[R] M)
  | n + 1 => ModuleCat.of R
      ((positiveTensorPowerModuleObj M n : Type (max u w)) ⊗[R] M)

attribute [reducible] positiveTensorPowerModuleObj

/-- The carrier of the positive tensor-power module object. -/
abbrev positiveTensorPower (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (n : ℕ) : Type (max u w) :=
  positiveTensorPowerModuleObj (R := R) M n

/-- The zero-indexed positive power is the tensor unit tensored with the
base module. -/
noncomputable def positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    positiveTensorPower (R := R) M 0 ≃ₗ[R] R ⊗[R] M := by
  with_reducible
    exact LinearEquiv.refl R _

/-- Splitting off the final factor of a positive tensor power. -/
noncomputable def positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n : ℕ) :
    positiveTensorPower (R := R) M (n + 1) ≃ₗ[R]
      positiveTensorPower (R := R) M n ⊗[R] M := by
  with_reducible
    exact LinearEquiv.refl R _

@[simp]
theorem positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv_apply
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (x : positiveTensorPower (R := R) M 0) :
    positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv M x = x :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv_symm_apply
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (x : R ⊗[R] M) :
    (positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv M).symm x = x :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv_apply
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n : ℕ)
    (x : positiveTensorPower (R := R) M (n + 1)) :
    positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv M n x = x :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv_symm_apply
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n : ℕ)
    (x : positiveTensorPower (R := R) M n ⊗[R] M) :
    (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv M n).symm x = x :=
  rfl

/-- The map on a positive tensor power induced by a linear map. -/
noncomputable def positiveTensorPowerMap
    {M : Type w} {N : Type x} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : ∀ n : ℕ,
      positiveTensorPower (R := R) M n →ₗ[R]
        positiveTensorPower (R := R) N n
  | 0 => LinearMap.lTensor R f
  | n + 1 => TensorProduct.map (positiveTensorPowerMap f n) f

attribute [reducible] positiveTensorPowerMap

@[simp]
theorem positiveTensorPowerMap_zero
    {M : Type w} {N : Type x} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    positiveTensorPowerMap f 0 = LinearMap.lTensor R f :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem positiveTensorPowerMap_succ
    {M : Type w} {N : Type x} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (n : ℕ) :
    positiveTensorPowerMap f (n + 1) =
      TensorProduct.map (positiveTensorPowerMap f n) f :=
  rfl

/-- Positive tensor powers preserve identity linear maps. -/
@[simp]
theorem positiveTensorPowerMap_id
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n : ℕ) :
    positiveTensorPowerMap (LinearMap.id (R := R) (M := M)) n =
      LinearMap.id := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact LinearMap.lTensor_id (R := R) R M
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [positiveTensorPowerMap_succ, ih, TensorProduct.map_id]

/-- Positive tensor powers preserve composition of linear maps. -/
theorem positiveTensorPowerMap_comp
    {M : Type w} {N : Type x} {P : Type y}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] P) (n : ℕ) :
    positiveTensorPowerMap (g.comp f) n =
      (positiveTensorPowerMap g n).comp
        (positiveTensorPowerMap f n) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact LinearMap.lTensor_comp (M := R) (f := f) (g := g)
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [positiveTensorPowerMap_succ, positiveTensorPowerMap_succ,
        positiveTensorPowerMap_succ, ih, TensorProduct.map_comp]

/-- A linear equivalence induces a linear equivalence on every positive
tensor power. -/
noncomputable def positiveTensorPowerCongr
    {M : Type w} {N : Type x}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) (n : ℕ) :
    positiveTensorPower (R := R) M n ≃ₗ[R]
      positiveTensorPower (R := R) N n :=
  LinearEquiv.ofLinearMap
    (positiveTensorPowerMap e.toLinearMap n)
    (positiveTensorPowerMap e.symm.toLinearMap n) (by
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro z
      change positiveTensorPowerMap e.toLinearMap n
          (positiveTensorPowerMap e.symm.toLinearMap n z) = z
      rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← positiveTensorPowerMap_comp]
      have hcomp : e.toLinearMap.comp e.symm.toLinearMap =
          LinearMap.id := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro y
        exact e.apply_symm_apply y
      rw [hcomp, positiveTensorPowerMap_id, LinearMap.id_apply]) (by
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro z
      change positiveTensorPowerMap e.symm.toLinearMap n
          (positiveTensorPowerMap e.toLinearMap n z) = z
      rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← positiveTensorPowerMap_comp]
      have hcomp : e.symm.toLinearMap.comp e.toLinearMap =
          LinearMap.id := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro y
        exact e.symm_apply_apply y
      rw [hcomp, positiveTensorPowerMap_id, LinearMap.id_apply])

@[simp]
theorem positiveTensorPowerCongr_apply
    {M : Type w} {N : Type x}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) (n : ℕ)
    (x : positiveTensorPower (R := R) M n) :
    positiveTensorPowerCongr e n x =
      positiveTensorPowerMap e.toLinearMap n x :=
  rfl

/-- Naturality of the zero-indexed positive-power splitting. -/
theorem positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv_naturality
    {M : Type w} {N : Type x} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (g : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    (positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv N).toLinearMap.comp
        (positiveTensorPowerMap g 0) =
      (LinearMap.lTensor R g).comp
        (positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv M).toLinearMap := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro z
  rfl

/-- Naturality of splitting off the final positive tensor-power factor. -/
theorem positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv_naturality
    {M : Type w} {N : Type x} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (g : M →ₗ[R] N) (n : ℕ) :
    (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv N n).toLinearMap.comp
        (positiveTensorPowerMap g (n + 1)) =
      (TensorProduct.map (positiveTensorPowerMap g n) g).comp
        (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv M n).toLinearMap := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro z
  rfl

variable {G : ι → Type w}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] [∀ i, Module R (G i)]
variable (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[R] G j)
variable [DirectedSystem G (f · · ·)]

/-- The transition map on a positive tensor power of a directed system. -/
noncomputable def positiveTensorPowerTransition
    (n : ℕ) (i j : ι) (hij : i ≤ j) :
    positiveTensorPower (R := R) (G i) n →ₗ[R]
      positiveTensorPower (R := R) (G j) n :=
  positiveTensorPowerMap (f i j hij) n

attribute [reducible] positiveTensorPowerTransition

omit [DecidableEq ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι]
  [DirectedSystem G (f · · ·)] in
/-- Successor splitting is natural for the stagewise transition, stated
with the canonical diagonal transition on the target system. -/
theorem positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv_transition_naturality
    (n : ℕ) (i j : ι) (hij : i ≤ j) :
    (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv (R := R) (G j) n).toLinearMap.comp
        (positiveTensorPowerTransition f (n + 1) i j hij) =
      (diagonalTransition
        (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) f i j hij).comp
        (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv (R := R) (G i) n).toLinearMap := by
  simpa only [positiveTensorPowerTransition, diagonalTransition] using
    positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv_naturality (f i j hij) n

/-- Every positive tensor power of a directed module system is again a
directed system. -/
instance positiveTensorPowerDirectedSystem (n : ℕ) :
    DirectedSystem
      (fun i => positiveTensorPower (R := R) (G i) n)
      (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n · · ·) where
  map_self i x := by
    have hself : f i i le_rfl = LinearMap.id := by
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro y
      exact DirectedSystem.map_self' f y
    rw [positiveTensorPowerTransition, hself,
      positiveTensorPowerMap_id, LinearMap.id_apply]
  map_map {k j i} hij hjk x := by
    have hcomp : (f j k hjk).comp (f i j hij) =
        f i k (hij.trans hjk) := by
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro y
      exact DirectedSystem.map_map' f hij hjk y
    change positiveTensorPowerMap (f j k hjk) n
        (positiveTensorPowerMap (f i j hij) n x) =
      positiveTensorPowerMap (f i k (hij.trans hjk)) n x
    rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← positiveTensorPowerMap_comp, hcomp]

/-- The direct limit of the positive tensor-power system is the same tensor
power of the original direct limit. -/
noncomputable def positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv : ∀ n : ℕ,
    Module.DirectLimit
        (fun i => positiveTensorPower (R := R) (G i) n)
        (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) ≃ₗ[R]
      positiveTensorPower (R := R) (Module.DirectLimit G f) n
  | 0 =>
      Module.DirectLimit.congr
          (fun i => positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv (G i))
          (fun i j hij =>
            positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv_naturality (f i j hij)) ≪≫ₗ
        (TensorProduct.directLimitRight f R).symm ≪≫ₗ
        (positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv
          (Module.DirectLimit G f)).symm
  | n + 1 =>
      Module.DirectLimit.congr
          (fun i => positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv (G i) n)
          (fun i j hij =>
            positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv_naturality (f i j hij) n) ≪≫ₗ
        directLimitDiagonal
          (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) f ≪≫ₗ
        TensorProduct.congr
          (positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv n)
          (LinearEquiv.refl R (Module.DirectLimit G f)) ≪≫ₗ
        (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv
          (Module.DirectLimit G f) n).symm

attribute [reducible] positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv

/-- The tensor-power direct-limit equivalence sends a stage representative
to the positive tensor power of the canonical stage map. -/
@[simp]
theorem positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv_apply_of :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ι)
      (x : positiveTensorPower (R := R) (G i) n),
      positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv f n
          (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
            (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) i x) =
        positiveTensorPowerMap
          (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i) n x
  | 0, i, x => by
      let stageEquiv := fun j =>
        positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv (R := R) (G j)
      let stageCongr := Module.DirectLimit.congr stageEquiv
        (fun a b hab =>
          positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv_naturality (f a b hab))
      calc
        positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv f 0
            (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
              (positiveTensorPowerTransition f 0) i x) =
          (positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv (R := R)
              (Module.DirectLimit G f)).symm
            ((TensorProduct.directLimitRight f R).symm
              (stageCongr
                (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
                  (positiveTensorPowerTransition f 0) i x))) := rfl
        _ = (positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv (R := R)
              (Module.DirectLimit G f)).symm
            ((TensorProduct.directLimitRight f R).symm
              (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
                (fun a b hab => LinearMap.lTensor R (f a b hab)) i
                (positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv (R := R) (G i) x))) := by
              rw [Module.DirectLimit.congr_apply_of]
        _ = positiveTensorPowerMap
            (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i) 0 x := by
              rw [positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv_apply,
                positiveTensorPowerZeroEquiv_symm_apply,
                positiveTensorPowerMap_zero]
              induction x using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
              | tmul r y =>
                  rw [TensorProduct.directLimitRight_symm_of_tmul,
                    LinearMap.lTensor_tmul]
              | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
  | n + 1, i, x => by
      let stageEquiv := fun j =>
        positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv (R := R) (G j) n
      let stageCongr := Module.DirectLimit.congr
        (f' := diagonalTransition
          (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) f) stageEquiv
        (fun a b hab =>
          positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv_transition_naturality
            f n a b hab)
      let diagonalEquiv := directLimitDiagonal
        (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) f
      let factorEquiv := TensorProduct.congr
        (positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv f n)
        (LinearEquiv.refl R (Module.DirectLimit G f))
      calc
        positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv f (n + 1)
            (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
              (positiveTensorPowerTransition f (n + 1)) i x) =
          (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv (R := R)
              (Module.DirectLimit G f) n).symm
            (factorEquiv
              (diagonalEquiv
                (stageCongr
                  (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
                    (positiveTensorPowerTransition f (n + 1)) i x)))) := rfl
        _ = (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv (R := R)
              (Module.DirectLimit G f) n).symm
            (factorEquiv
              (diagonalEquiv
                (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
                  (diagonalTransition
                    (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) f) i
                  (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv (R := R) (G i) n x)))) := by
              dsimp only [stageCongr]
              rw [Module.DirectLimit.congr_apply_of]
        _ = (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv (R := R)
              (Module.DirectLimit G f) n).symm
            (factorEquiv
              (TensorProduct.map
                (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
                  (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) i)
                (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i)
                (positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv (R := R) (G i) n x))) := by
              rw [directLimitDiagonal_of]
        _ = positiveTensorPowerMap
            (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i) (n + 1) x := by
              rw [positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv_apply,
                positiveTensorPowerSuccEquiv_symm_apply,
                positiveTensorPowerMap_succ]
              change TensorProduct.map
                  (positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv f n).toLinearMap
                  (LinearEquiv.refl R
                    (Module.DirectLimit G f)).toLinearMap
                  (TensorProduct.map
                    (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
                      (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) i)
                    (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i) x) = _
              rw [TensorProduct.map_map]
              have hleft :
                  (positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv f n).toLinearMap.comp
                      (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
                        (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) i) =
                    positiveTensorPowerMap
                      (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i) n := by
                apply LinearMap.ext
                intro y
                exact positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv_apply_of n i y
              rw [hleft, LinearEquiv.refl_toLinearMap, LinearMap.id_comp]

/-- Eventual-zero detection for every positive tensor power of a directed
module system. -/
theorem exists_eq_zero_of_positiveTensorPowerMap_to_directLimit_eq_zero
    {i : ι} (n : ℕ)
    (x : positiveTensorPower (R := R) (G i) n)
    (hx : positiveTensorPowerMap
      (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i) n x = 0) :
    ∃ j : ι, ∃ hij : i ≤ j,
      positiveTensorPowerTransition f n i j hij x = 0 := by
  have hcolimit :
      Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _
        (positiveTensorPowerTransition f n) i x = 0 := by
    apply (positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv f n).injective
    rw [positiveTensorPowerDirectLimitEquiv_apply_of, map_zero]
    exact hx
  exact Module.DirectLimit.of.zero_exact hcolimit

end TensorProduct

module

public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.FaithfullyFlat.Algebra
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Tower

/-!
# Original tensor Čech exactness under faithfully flat scalar extension

The unit sends m to 1 tensor m. The original overlap difference sends
b tensor m to b tensor (1 tensor m) minus 1 tensor (b tensor m).
After genuine scalar extension, multiplication of the first two coefficients
contracts the complex. Faithful flatness reflects its exactness.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

namespace TensorProduct

open scoped TensorProduct

universe u v w
variable (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (M : Type w)
variable [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]

/-- The original coefficient-tensor unit. -/
def cechUnit : M →ₗ[A] B ⊗[A] M := TensorProduct.mk A B M 1

/-- The actual difference of the two original tensor overlap maps, in source order. -/
def cechDifference : (B ⊗[A] M) →ₗ[A] B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] M) :=
  (cechUnit A B M).lTensor B - TensorProduct.mk A B (B ⊗[A] M) 1

/-- The overlap difference retains its two actual tensor values with the original sign. -/
theorem cechDifference_tmul (b : B) (m : M) :
    cechDifference A B M (b ⊗ₜ[A] m) =
      b ⊗ₜ[A] ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] m) - (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (b ⊗ₜ[A] m) := by
  rw [cechDifference, LinearMap.sub_apply, LinearMap.lTensor_tmul]
  rfl

/-- Actual multiplication of the outer tensor coefficient on the original scalar-extended module. -/
def cechScalarAction : B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] M) →ₗ[A] B ⊗[A] M :=
  ((LinearMap.id : (B ⊗[A] M) →ₗ[A] B ⊗[A] M).liftBaseChange B).restrictScalars A

/-- The actual coefficient contraction multiplies the first two coefficients, preserving the original module. -/
theorem cechScalarAction_tmul (b c : B) (m : M) :
    cechScalarAction A B M (b ⊗ₜ[A] (c ⊗ₜ[A] m)) = (b * c) ⊗ₜ[A] m := by
  rw [cechScalarAction, LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul,
    LinearMap.id_apply, TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul]

/-- The original tensor overlap difference annihilates the original tensor unit. -/
theorem cechDifference_comp_unit : (cechDifference A B M).comp (cechUnit A B M) = 0 := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro m
  change cechDifference A B M ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A] m) = 0
  rw [cechDifference_tmul, sub_self]

/-- Multiplying the first two coefficients contracts the genuine scalar-extended overlap differential. -/
theorem cechScalarAction_comp_lTensor_difference :
    (cechScalarAction A B (B ⊗[A] M)).comp ((cechDifference A B M).lTensor B) =
      ((cechUnit A B M).lTensor B).comp (cechScalarAction A B M) - LinearMap.id := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro b x
  induction x using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | add x y hx hy =>
    simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.sub_apply,
      LinearMap.id_apply] at hx hy ⊢
    rw [hx, hy]
  | tmul c m =>
    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.sub_apply, LinearMap.id_apply,
      LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, cechDifference_tmul, TensorProduct.tmul_sub, map_sub,
      cechScalarAction_tmul, cechUnit, TensorProduct.mk_apply, mul_one]

/-- The original tensor Čech complex is exact after actual scalar extension. -/
theorem cech_lTensor_exact :
    Function.Exact ((cechUnit A B M).lTensor B) ((cechDifference A B M).lTensor B) := by
  have hcomp : ((cechDifference A B M).lTensor B).comp ((cechUnit A B M).lTensor B) = 0 := by
    rw [← LinearMap.lTensor_comp, cechDifference_comp_unit, LinearMap.lTensor_zero]
  intro x
  constructor
  · intro hx
    refine ⟨cechScalarAction A B M x, ?_⟩
    have h := LinearMap.congr_fun (cechScalarAction_comp_lTensor_difference A B M) x
    change cechScalarAction A B (B ⊗[A] M) ((cechDifference A B M).lTensor B x) =
      (cechUnit A B M).lTensor B (cechScalarAction A B M x) - x at h
    rw [hx, map_zero] at h
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp h.symm
  · rintro ⟨y, hy⟩
    rw [← hy]
    simpa only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply] using LinearMap.congr_fun hcomp y

/-- Faithful flatness reflects the exactness of the original, unaltered tensor Čech complex. -/
theorem cech_exact [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B] :
    Function.Exact (cechUnit A B M) (cechDifference A B M) :=
  Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_reflects_exact A B (cechUnit A B M) (cechDifference A B M)
    (cech_lTensor_exact A B M)

/-- The original module injects through its actual tensor unit under faithful flatness. -/
theorem cechUnit_injective [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B] : Function.Injective (cechUnit A B M) :=
  Module.FaithfullyFlat.tensorProduct_mk_injective M

end TensorProduct

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Pi
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Map
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.Projective
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.LinearMap.RetractComparison

/-!
# Hom–tensor comparison for a finite-projective tensor factor

The first Hom source is arbitrary. A genuine native finite-free retraction of
the tensor factor, together with the original coefficient-map naturality,
earns invertibility. Native finite product/tensor and Hom/product coordinates
compute the finite-free case. No basis or desired comparison is caller data.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe uR uP uN uU uV

variable (R : Type uR) [CommRing R]
  (P : Type uP) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
  (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]

attribute [local ext high] TensorProduct.ext

/-- Original coefficient-map naturality in the actual tensor factor. -/
theorem homTensorCoefficient_naturality
    {U : Type uU} {V : Type uV}
    [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U] [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V]
    (g : U →ₗ[R] V) :
    (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N V).comp (g.lTensor (P →ₗ[R] N)) =
      ((g.lTensor N).compRight R).comp (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N U) := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro f u
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro p
  rfl

/-- The canonical Hom–tensor map is bijective for a native finite-free tensor
factor. The Hom source remains unrestricted. -/
theorem homTensorFiniteFree_bijective (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N (Fin n → R)) := by
  let e : (P →ₗ[R] N) ⊗[R] (Fin n → R) ≃ₗ[R] (Fin n → (P →ₗ[R] N)) :=
    TensorProduct.piScalarRight R R (P →ₗ[R] N) (Fin n)
  let t : (P →ₗ[R] N ⊗[R] (Fin n → R)) ≃ₗ[R] (Fin n → (P →ₗ[R] N)) :=
    (LinearEquiv.refl R P).arrowCongr (TensorProduct.piScalarRight R R N (Fin n)) ≪≫ₗ
      (LinearEquiv.linearMapPi R (R := R) (M₂ := P) (φ := fun _ : Fin n => N)).symm
  have he : t.toLinearMap.comp (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N (Fin n → R)) =
      e.toLinearMap := by
    apply TensorProduct.ext'
    intro f u
    funext i
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro p
    change (TensorProduct.piScalarRight R R N (Fin n)
        ((rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N (Fin n → R) (f ⊗ₜ[R] u)) p)) i =
      (TensorProduct.piScalarRight R R (P →ₗ[R] N) (Fin n) (f ⊗ₜ[R] u)) i p
    rw [rTensorHomToHomRTensor_apply]
    simp only [TensorProduct.piScalarRight_apply, TensorProduct.piScalarRightHom_tmul,
      LinearMap.smul_apply]
  have hb : Function.Bijective
      (fun x => t (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N (Fin n → R) x)) := by
    change Function.Bijective (t.toLinearMap.comp
      (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N (Fin n → R)))
    rw [he]
    exact e.bijective
  constructor
  · intro x y h
    exact hb.injective (congrArg t h)
  · intro y
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hb.surjective (t y)
    exact ⟨x, t.injective hx⟩

/-- A genuine finite-projective tensor factor earns bijectivity of the original
canonical coefficient map by its native finite-free retraction. -/
theorem homTensorFiniteFactor_bijective
    (U : Type uU) [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U]
    [Module.Finite R U] [Module.Projective R U] :
    Function.Bijective (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N U) := by
  obtain ⟨n, f, g, hf, hg, hfg⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective R U
  let dF := f.lTensor (P →ₗ[R] N)
  let dG := g.lTensor (P →ₗ[R] N)
  let cF := (f.lTensor N).compRight R (M := P)
  let cG := (g.lTensor N).compRight R (M := P)
  have hd : dF.comp dG = LinearMap.id := by
    rw [← LinearMap.lTensor_comp, hfg, LinearMap.lTensor_id]
  have hfgN : (f.lTensor N).comp (g.lTensor N) = LinearMap.id := by
    rw [← LinearMap.lTensor_comp, hfg, LinearMap.lTensor_id]
  have hc : cF.comp cG = LinearMap.id := by
    ext h p
    change (f.lTensor N) ((g.lTensor N) (h p)) = h p
    exact LinearMap.congr_fun hfgN (h p)
  have hFree := homTensorFiniteFree_bijective R P N n
  have hNatF := homTensorCoefficient_naturality R P N f
  have hNatG := homTensorCoefficient_naturality R P N g
  exact LinearMap.comparison_bijective_of_retract
    (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N U)
    (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N (Fin n → R))
    dG dF cG cF hd hc hNatG hNatF hFree

/-- Actual original coefficient Iso; its forward map is the canonical map by
construction, rather than an arbitrary finite-projective comparison. -/
def homTensorFiniteFactorEquiv
    (U : Type uU) [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U]
    [Module.Finite R U] [Module.Projective R U] :
    (P →ₗ[R] N) ⊗[R] U ≃ₗ[R] P →ₗ[R] N ⊗[R] U :=
  LinearEquiv.ofBijective (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N U)
    (homTensorFiniteFactor_bijective R P N U)

theorem homTensorFiniteFactorEquiv_toLinearMap
    (U : Type uU) [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U]
    [Module.Finite R U] [Module.Projective R U] :
    (homTensorFiniteFactorEquiv R P N U).toLinearMap =
      rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N U := rfl

end TensorProduct

module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.HomFiniteFactor
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.SurjectiveScalarHom

/-!
# Original scalar transport for a finite-projective tensor factor

The unchanged scalar coordinate factors transport the coefficient equivalence
earned from the actual finite-free retraction of the tensor factor. The first
Hom source is arbitrary, and the hom is the original R coefficient map.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe uR uS uP uN uU

variable {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
  {P : Type uP} {N : Type uN} {U : Type uU}
  [AddCommGroup P] [AddCommGroup N] [AddCommGroup U]
  [Module R P] [Module R N] [Module R U]
  [Module S P] [Module S N] [Module S U]
  [IsScalarTower R S P] [IsScalarTower R S N] [IsScalarTower R S U]

/-- Original scalar/input/output Isos surround the actual finite-factor
coefficient equivalence. No finite-projectivity of the Hom source is required. -/
def homTensorFiniteFactorEquivOfSurjectiveScalars
    [Module.Finite S U] [Module.Projective S U]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    (P →ₗ[R] N) ⊗[R] U ≃ₗ[R] P →ₗ[R] N ⊗[R] U :=
  rTensorHomScalarInputEquiv h ≪≫ₗ
    (homTensorFiniteFactorEquiv S P N U).restrictScalars R ≪≫ₗ
      rTensorHomScalarOutputEquiv h

/-- Every original pure tensor retains its actual coefficient evaluation. -/
theorem homTensorFiniteFactorEquivOfSurjectiveScalars_tmul
    [Module.Finite S U] [Module.Projective S U]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) (f : P →ₗ[R] N) (u : U) (p : P) :
    homTensorFiniteFactorEquivOfSurjectiveScalars (P := P) (N := N) (U := U) h
        (f ⊗ₜ[R] u) p = f p ⊗ₜ[R] u := by
  simp [homTensorFiniteFactorEquivOfSurjectiveScalars, homTensorFiniteFactorEquiv,
    rTensorHomScalarInputEquiv, rTensorHomScalarOutputEquiv,
    TensorProduct.congr_tmul, TensorProduct.rTensorHomToHomRTensor_apply,
    TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul, LinearEquiv.arrowCongr,
    LinearMap.extendScalarsOfSurjectiveEquiv]

/-- The source map is exactly the original R coefficient comparison, with the
scalar quotient and its actual inverse completely internal to the construction. -/
theorem homTensorFiniteFactorEquivOfSurjectiveScalars_toLinearMap
    [Module.Finite S U] [Module.Projective S U]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    (homTensorFiniteFactorEquivOfSurjectiveScalars (P := P) (N := N) (U := U) h).toLinearMap =
      rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N U := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro f u
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro p
  change homTensorFiniteFactorEquivOfSurjectiveScalars (P := P) (N := N) (U := U) h
      (f ⊗ₜ[R] u) p = rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) P N U (f ⊗ₜ[R] u) p
  rw [homTensorFiniteFactorEquivOfSurjectiveScalars_tmul,
    TensorProduct.rTensorHomToHomRTensor_apply]

end TensorProduct

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.VectorSpace
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Basis
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Map

/-!
# Faithfulness of the algebraic tensor action on linear maps

The canonical tensor evaluation maps are injective over a field. Coordinates
in a basis of the vector factor detect every coefficient linear map. Applying
this twice proves faithfulness of the tensor action on two spaces, without
finite-dimension assumptions.

This injectivity supplies the algebraic faithfulness needed by tensor
representations and completion maps.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe uR uM uN uP uM₂ uN₂

variable {R : Type uR} [Field R]
variable {M : Type uM} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
variable {N : Type uN} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
variable {P : Type uP} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]

/-- Tensoring vectors with linear maps gives a faithful pointwise tensor action. -/
theorem lTensorHomToHomLTensor_injective :
    Function.Injective (lTensorHomToHomLTensor (RingHom.id R) P M N) := by
  classical
  let b := Module.Basis.ofVectorSpace R M
  have hcoord (z : M ⊗[R] (P →ₗ[R] N)) (i : Module.Basis.ofVectorSpaceIndex R M) (p : P) :
      (equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft (N := P →ₗ[R] N) b z i) p =
        equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft (N := N) b
          (lTensorHomToHomLTensor (RingHom.id R) P M N z p) i := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul m f =>
      simp only [equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft_apply_tmul_apply,
        lTensorHomToHomLTensor_apply, LinearMap.smul_apply]
    | add z w hz hw =>
      simp only [map_add, Finsupp.add_apply, LinearMap.add_apply, hz, hw]
  intro z w h
  apply (equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft (N := P →ₗ[R] N) b).injective
  apply Finsupp.ext
  intro i
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro p
  have hc := congrArg
    (fun f : P →ₗ[R] M ⊗[R] N => equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft (N := N) b (f p) i) h
  rw [← hcoord z i p, ← hcoord w i p] at hc
  exact hc

/-- Tensoring linear maps with vectors also gives a faithful tensor action. -/
theorem rTensorHomToHomRTensor_injective :
    Function.Injective (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (RingHom.id R) P M N) := by
  have hflip (z : (P →ₗ[R] M) ⊗[R] N) (p : P) :
      TensorProduct.comm R N M
        (lTensorHomToHomLTensor (RingHom.id R) P N M
          (TensorProduct.comm R (P →ₗ[R] M) N z) p) =
        rTensorHomToHomRTensor (RingHom.id R) P M N z p := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul f n =>
      simp only [comm_tmul, lTensorHomToHomLTensor_apply, rTensorHomToHomRTensor_apply]
    | add z w hz hw =>
      simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hz, hw]
  intro z w h
  apply (TensorProduct.comm R (P →ₗ[R] M) N).injective
  apply lTensorHomToHomLTensor_injective
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro p
  apply (TensorProduct.comm R N M).injective
  rw [hflip, hflip]
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun h p

variable {M₂ : Type uM₂} [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
variable {N₂ : Type uN₂} [AddCommGroup N₂] [Module R N₂]

/-- The tensor product of two linear maps acts faithfully on the algebraic tensor of their inputs. -/
theorem homTensorHomMap_injective :
    Function.Injective (homTensorHomMap (RingHom.id R) M N M₂ N₂) := by
  have heval (z : (M →ₗ[R] M₂) ⊗[R] (N →ₗ[R] N₂)) (m : M) (n : N) :
      homTensorHomMap (RingHom.id R) M N M₂ N₂ z (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) =
        lTensorHomToHomLTensor (RingHom.id R) N M₂ N₂
          (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (RingHom.id R) M M₂ (N →ₗ[R] N₂) z m) n := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul f g =>
      simp only [homTensorHomMap_apply, map_tmul,
        rTensorHomToHomRTensor_apply, lTensorHomToHomLTensor_apply]
    | add z w hz hw =>
      simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hz, hw]
  intro z w h
  apply rTensorHomToHomRTensor_injective
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro m
  apply lTensorHomToHomLTensor_injective
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro n
  have he := DFunLike.congr_fun h (m ⊗ₜ[R] n)
  rw [heval, heval] at he
  exact he

end TensorProduct

module
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Basic

/-! # Actual integer torsion through the existing tensor product -/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false
universe u v w
open scoped TensorProduct
namespace TensorProduct
variable {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R]
  {M : Type v} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  {N : Type w} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N]

/-- Torsion of the first actual factor kills every vector of the existing tensor product. -/
theorem nsmul_eq_zero_of_left (m : ℕ) (hM : ∀ x : M, m • x = 0) (x : M ⊗[R] N) :
    m • x = 0 := by
  induction x using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul a b => rw [smul_tmul', hM a, zero_tmul]
  | add a b ha hb => rw [nsmul_add, ha, hb, add_zero]

/-- Torsion of the second actual factor kills every vector of the existing tensor product. -/
theorem nsmul_eq_zero_of_right (m : ℕ) (hN : ∀ x : N, m • x = 0) (x : M ⊗[R] N) :
    m • x = 0 := by
  induction x using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul a b => rw [← tmul_smul, hN b, tmul_zero]
  | add a b ha hb => rw [nsmul_add, ha, hb, add_zero]

end TensorProduct

module
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Map
public import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.ULift

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false
universe v w p q s
open TensorProduct

namespace ScalarRestriction

variable (ell : ℕ) (M : Type v) (N : Type w)
  [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
  [Module (ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)) M] [Module (ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)) N]

/-- Integer balancing implies balancing over the actual lifted residue ring. -/
theorem liftedZModIntegerCompatibleSMul :
    TensorProduct.CompatibleSMul ℤ (ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)) M N := by
  refine ⟨?_⟩
  intro a m n
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := ZMod.intCast_surjective a.down
  have ha : (z : ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)) = a := by
    apply ULift.ext
    exact hz
  rw [← ha, Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul, Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul]
  exact TensorProduct.smul_tmul z m n

/-- The original residue-ring tensor and its integer tensor have the same pure tensors. -/
def liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv :
    M ⊗[ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)] N ≃ₗ[ℤ] M ⊗[ℤ] N := by
  let : TensorProduct.CompatibleSMul ℤ (ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)) M N :=
    liftedZModIntegerCompatibleSMul ell M N
  exact TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul ℤ (ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)) ℤ M N

@[simp]
theorem liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv_tmul (m : M) (n : N) :
    liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv ell M N (m ⊗ₜ[ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)] n) =
      m ⊗ₜ[ℤ] n := rfl

@[simp]
theorem liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv_symm_tmul (m : M) (n : N) :
    (liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv ell M N).symm (m ⊗ₜ[ℤ] n) =
      m ⊗ₜ[ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)] n := rfl

variable {M N} {P : Type p} {Q : Type q}
  [AddCommGroup P] [AddCommGroup Q]
  [Module (ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)) P] [Module (ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)) Q]

/-- Both original factor maps commute with the computed integer tensor comparison. -/
theorem liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv_naturality
    (f : M →ₗ[ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)] P) (g : N →ₗ[ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)] Q) :
    (TensorProduct.map (f.restrictScalars ℤ) (g.restrictScalars ℤ)).comp
        (liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv ell M N).toLinearMap =
      (liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv ell P Q).toLinearMap.comp
        ((TensorProduct.map f g).restrictScalars ℤ) := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  induction x using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul m n => rfl
  | add x y hx hy =>
      let lhsMap : M ⊗[ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)] N →ₗ[ℤ] P ⊗[ℤ] Q :=
        (TensorProduct.map (f.restrictScalars ℤ) (g.restrictScalars ℤ)).comp
          (liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv ell M N).toLinearMap
      let rhsMap : M ⊗[ULift.{s} (ZMod ell)] N →ₗ[ℤ] P ⊗[ℤ] Q :=
        (liftedZModIntegerTensorEquiv ell P Q).toLinearMap.comp
          ((TensorProduct.map f g).restrictScalars ℤ)
      have hx' : lhsMap x = rhsMap x := hx
      have hy' : lhsMap y = rhsMap y := hy
      exact (lhsMap.map_add x y).trans
        ((congrArg₂ (· + ·) hx' hy').trans (rhsMap.map_add x y).symm)

end ScalarRestriction

module

public import Mathlib.RingTheory.IsTensorProduct
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Tower

/-!
# Mixed base change over an original integer tensor product

Two independent coefficient rings act through their original inclusions in
their integer tensor product. Cancelling the two scalar extensions gives
the actual original tensor of the two coefficient modules. The construction
uses canonical tensor pushouts and does not require flatness or freeness.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule

universe u v w z
variable (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
variable (M : Type w) (N : Type z) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N]

attribute [local instance] Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
attribute [local instance] SMulCommClass.of_commMonoid

local notation "T" => R ⊗[ℤ] S
local notation "L" => T ⊗[R] M
local notation "Q" => T ⊗[S] N

local instance mixedBaseChangeSwappedPushout : Algebra.IsPushout ℤ S R T :=
  (inferInstance : Algebra.IsPushout ℤ R S T).symm

local instance mixedBaseChangeIntTower (P : Type*) [AddCommGroup P] [Module T P] :
    IsScalarTower ℤ T P := AddCommGroup.intIsScalarTower

private def mixedCancelRight : L ⊗[T] Q ≃ₗ[T] L ⊗[S] N :=
  (TensorProduct.isBaseChange S N T).tensorEquiv L

private def mixedCancelLeft : L ⊗[S] N ≃ₗ[S] N ⊗[ℤ] M :=
  (TensorProduct.congr (Algebra.IsPushout.cancelBaseChange ℤ S R T M) (LinearEquiv.refl S N)).trans
    ((TensorProduct.comm S (S ⊗[ℤ] M) N).trans (cancelBaseChange ℤ S S N M))

/-- The mixed scalar extensions cancel to the original integer tensor of the modules. -/
@[no_expose]
def mixedBaseChangeEquiv : L ⊗[T] Q ≃ₗ[ℤ] M ⊗[ℤ] N :=
  ((mixedCancelRight R S M N).restrictScalars ℤ).trans
    (((mixedCancelLeft R S M N).restrictScalars ℤ).trans (TensorProduct.comm ℤ N M))

private theorem mixedCancelRight_symm_tmul (x : L) (n : N) :
    (mixedCancelRight R S M N).symm (x ⊗ₜ[S] n) = x ⊗ₜ[T] ((1 : T) ⊗ₜ[S] n) := by
  unfold mixedCancelRight IsBaseChange.tensorEquiv
  rw [LinearEquiv.symm_trans_apply, cancelBaseChange_symm_tmul, LinearEquiv.symm_lTensor,
    LinearEquiv.symm_symm, LinearEquiv.lTensor_tmul, IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul, one_smul]
  rfl

private theorem mixedCancelLeft_symm_tmul (m : M) (n : N) :
    (mixedCancelLeft R S M N).symm (n ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = ((1 : T) ⊗ₜ[R] m) ⊗ₜ[S] n := by
  unfold mixedCancelLeft
  simp only [LinearEquiv.symm_trans_apply]
  rw [cancelBaseChange_symm_tmul, TensorProduct.comm_symm, TensorProduct.comm_tmul,
    TensorProduct.congr_symm, TensorProduct.congr_tmul,
    LinearEquiv.refl_symm, LinearEquiv.refl_apply, Algebra.IsPushout.cancelBaseChange_symm_tmul, map_one]

/-- The inverse retains the literal original tensor, inserting only the two unit coefficients. -/
theorem mixedBaseChangeEquiv_symm_tmul (m : M) (n : N) :
    (mixedBaseChangeEquiv R S M N).symm (m ⊗ₜ[ℤ] n) =
      ((1 : T) ⊗ₜ[R] m) ⊗ₜ[T] ((1 : T) ⊗ₜ[S] n) := by
  unfold mixedBaseChangeEquiv
  simp only [LinearEquiv.symm_trans_apply]
  change (mixedCancelRight R S M N).symm
    ((mixedCancelLeft R S M N).symm ((TensorProduct.comm ℤ N M).symm (m ⊗ₜ[ℤ] n))) = _
  rw [TensorProduct.comm_symm, TensorProduct.comm_tmul, mixedCancelLeft_symm_tmul,
    mixedCancelRight_symm_tmul]

/-- The canonical unit tensors recover the original module tensor. -/
theorem mixedBaseChangeEquiv_unit_tmul (m : M) (n : N) :
    mixedBaseChangeEquiv R S M N
      (((1 : T) ⊗ₜ[R] m) ⊗ₜ[T] ((1 : T) ⊗ₜ[S] n)) = m ⊗ₜ[ℤ] n := by
  rw [← mixedBaseChangeEquiv_symm_tmul, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]

end TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Bimodule
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.LinearMap.Basic

/-!
# Maps for the native tensor-product module action

The module structures are the native `TensorProduct.Algebra.module` values
computed from the original two scalar actions. A ground-linear equivariant
map is linear for their tensor product, and a tensor-product-linear map is
linear for each original action. No module structure is supplied as data.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

open scoped TensorProduct

universe u a b m n p

namespace TensorProduct.Algebra

variable {k : Type u} [CommSemiring k]
  {A : Type a} {B : Type b} [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
  [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B]
  {M : Type m} {N : Type n}
  [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N]
  [Module k M] [Module k N]
  [Module A M] [Module A N] [Module B M] [Module B N]
  [IsScalarTower k A M] [IsScalarTower k A N]
  [IsScalarTower k B M] [IsScalarTower k B N]
  [SMulCommClass A B M] [SMulCommClass A B N]

/-- Package the original equivariant ground map over the native tensor scalars. -/
def ofLinearMap (f : M →ₗ[k] N)
    (hA : ∀ (a : A) (x : M), f (a • x) = a • f x)
    (hB : ∀ (b : B) (x : M), f (b • x) = b • f x) :
    letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
    letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
    M →ₗ[A ⊗[k] B] N := by
  letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  refine { toFun := f, map_add' := f.map_add, map_smul' := ?_ }
  intro z x
  change f (z • x) = z • f x
  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul a b => rw [smul_def, smul_def, hA, hB]
  | add z w hz hw => rw [add_smul, f.map_add, hz, hw, add_smul]

@[simp]
theorem ofLinearMap_apply (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (hA hB) (x : M) :
    ofLinearMap (k := k) (A := A) (B := B) f hA hB x = f x := rfl

/-- A tensor-module morphism preserves the original first scalar action. -/
def toLeftLinearMap
    (f : letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      M →ₗ[A ⊗[k] B] N) : M →ₗ[A] N := by
  letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  refine { toFun := f, map_add' := f.map_add, map_smul' := ?_ }
  intro a x
  simpa only [RingHom.id_apply, smul_def, one_smul] using f.map_smul (a ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : B)) x

/-- A tensor-module morphism preserves the original second scalar action. -/
def toRightLinearMap
    (f : letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      M →ₗ[A ⊗[k] B] N) : M →ₗ[B] N := by
  letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  refine { toFun := f, map_add' := f.map_add, map_smul' := ?_ }
  intro b x
  simpa only [RingHom.id_apply, smul_def, one_smul] using f.map_smul ((1 : A) ⊗ₜ[k] b) x

@[simp]
theorem toLeftLinearMap_apply
    (f : letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      M →ₗ[A ⊗[k] B] N) (x : M) : toLeftLinearMap f x = f x := rfl

@[simp]
theorem toRightLinearMap_apply
    (f : letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      M →ₗ[A ⊗[k] B] N) (x : M) : toRightLinearMap f x = f x := rfl

/-- Returning through the first action retains the original ground dictionary. -/
@[simp]
theorem toLeftLinearMap_ofLinearMap (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (hA hB) :
    (toLeftLinearMap (k := k) (A := A) (B := B)
      (ofLinearMap (k := k) (A := A) (B := B) f hA hB)).restrictScalars k = f := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  rfl

/-- Returning through the second action also retains the same ground map. -/
@[simp]
theorem toRightLinearMap_ofLinearMap (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (hA hB) :
    (toRightLinearMap (k := k) (A := A) (B := B)
      (ofLinearMap (k := k) (A := A) (B := B) f hA hB)).restrictScalars k = f := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  rfl

end TensorProduct.Algebra

module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.ModuleMap
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.Maps

/-!
# Semilinear maps for native tensor-product module actions

The two endpoint algebras may change independently and need not commute
internally. Equivariance under their actual commuting actions is equivalent
to semilinearity under the native tensor ring map. The source and target
module carriers retain their independent universes and their given ground
modules. No category of artificial bundled bimodules is introduced.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

open scoped TensorProduct

universe u a a' a'' b b' b'' m n p

namespace TensorProduct.Algebra

variable {k : Type u} [CommSemiring k]
  {A : Type a} {A' : Type a'} {B : Type b} {B' : Type b'}
  [Semiring A] [Semiring A'] [Semiring B] [Semiring B']
  [Algebra k A] [Algebra k A'] [Algebra k B] [Algebra k B']
  {M : Type m} {N : Type n}
  [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module k M] [Module k N]
  [Module A M] [Module B M] [Module A' N] [Module B' N]
  [IsScalarTower k A M] [IsScalarTower k B M]
  [IsScalarTower k A' N] [IsScalarTower k B' N]
  [SMulCommClass A B M] [SMulCommClass A' B' N]

/-- An equivariant ground map is semilinear for the actual native tensor ring map. -/
def ofSemilinearMap (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B') (f : M →ₗ[k] N)
    (hA : ∀ (a : A) (x : M), f (a • x) = φ a • f x)
    (hB : ∀ (b : B) (x : M), f (b • x) = ψ b • f x) :
    letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
    letI : Module (A' ⊗[k] B') N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
    M →ₛₗ[(Algebra.TensorProduct.map φ ψ).toRingHom] N := by
  letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  letI : Module (A' ⊗[k] B') N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  refine { toFun := f, map_add' := f.map_add, map_smul' := ?_ }
  intro z x
  change f (z • x) = Algebra.TensorProduct.map φ ψ z • f x
  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul a b => rw [smul_def, Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, smul_def, hA, hB]
  | add z w hz hw => rw [add_smul, f.map_add, hz, hw, map_add, add_smul]

/-- The semilinear tensor-module map keeps the supplied original function. -/
theorem ofSemilinearMap_apply (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B')
    (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (hA hB) (x : M) :
    ofSemilinearMap φ ψ f hA hB x = f x := rfl

/-- Native tensor semilinearity implies semilinearity under the first original action. -/
def toLeftSemilinearMap (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B')
    (f : letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      letI : Module (A' ⊗[k] B') N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      M →ₛₗ[(Algebra.TensorProduct.map φ ψ).toRingHom] N) :
    M →ₛₗ[φ.toRingHom] N := by
  letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  letI : Module (A' ⊗[k] B') N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  refine { toFun := f, map_add' := f.map_add, map_smul' := ?_ }
  intro a x
  have h := f.map_smul' (a ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : B)) x
  change f ((a ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : B)) • x) =
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map φ ψ (a ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : B))) • f x at h
  change f (a • x) = φ a • f x
  simpa only [Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, map_one, smul_def, one_smul] using h

/-- Native tensor semilinearity likewise preserves the second original action. -/
def toRightSemilinearMap (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B')
    (f : letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      letI : Module (A' ⊗[k] B') N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      M →ₛₗ[(Algebra.TensorProduct.map φ ψ).toRingHom] N) :
    M →ₛₗ[ψ.toRingHom] N := by
  letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  letI : Module (A' ⊗[k] B') N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
  refine { toFun := f, map_add' := f.map_add, map_smul' := ?_ }
  intro b x
  have h := f.map_smul' ((1 : A) ⊗ₜ[k] b) x
  change f (((1 : A) ⊗ₜ[k] b) • x) =
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map φ ψ ((1 : A) ⊗ₜ[k] b)) • f x at h
  change f (b • x) = ψ b • f x
  simpa only [Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, map_one, smul_def, one_smul] using h

/-- The endpoint algebra maps retain the original ground-linear function. -/
def toGroundLinearMap (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B')
    (f : letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      letI : Module (A' ⊗[k] B') N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
      M →ₛₗ[(Algebra.TensorProduct.map φ ψ).toRingHom] N) : M →ₗ[k] N := by
  let h := toLeftSemilinearMap φ ψ f
  refine { toFun := h, map_add' := h.map_add, map_smul' := ?_ }
  intro c x
  have hx := h.map_smulₛₗ (algebraMap k A c) x
  change h ((algebraMap k A c) • x) = φ (algebraMap k A c) • h x at hx
  simpa only [φ.commutes, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul, RingHom.id_apply] using hx

/-- The two endpoint equations characterize a native semilinear bimodule map. -/
def semilinearMapEquiv (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B') :
    (letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
     letI : Module (A' ⊗[k] B') N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
     M →ₛₗ[(Algebra.TensorProduct.map φ ψ).toRingHom] N) ≃
    {f : M →ₗ[k] N //
      (∀ (a : A) (x : M), f (a • x) = φ a • f x) ∧
        (∀ (b : B) (x : M), f (b • x) = ψ b • f x)} where
  toFun f := ⟨toGroundLinearMap φ ψ f,
    fun a x => (toLeftSemilinearMap φ ψ f).map_smulₛₗ a x,
    fun b x => by
      dsimp only [toGroundLinearMap, toLeftSemilinearMap]
      have h := (toRightSemilinearMap φ ψ f).map_smul' b x
      change f (b • x) = ψ b • f x at h
      exact h⟩
  invFun f := ofSemilinearMap φ ψ f.1 f.2.1 f.2.2
  left_inv f := by
    letI : Module (A ⊗[k] B) M := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
    letI : Module (A' ⊗[k] B') N := TensorProduct.Algebra.module
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro x
    rfl
  right_inv f := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro x
    rfl

/-- Reading the first action after constructing the tensor map changes no values. -/
theorem toLeftSemilinearMap_ofSemilinearMap (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B')
    (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (hA hB) (x : M) :
    toLeftSemilinearMap φ ψ (ofSemilinearMap φ ψ f hA hB) x = f x := rfl

/-- Reading the second action has the same identity on original values. -/
theorem toRightSemilinearMap_ofSemilinearMap (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B')
    (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (hA hB) (x : M) :
    toRightSemilinearMap φ ψ (ofSemilinearMap φ ψ f hA hB) x = f x := rfl

/-- The same supplied ground-module dictionary is recovered exactly. -/
theorem toGroundLinearMap_ofSemilinearMap (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B')
    (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (hA hB) :
    toGroundLinearMap φ ψ (ofSemilinearMap φ ψ f hA hB) = f := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  rfl

section Composition

variable {A'' : Type a''} {B'' : Type b''} [Semiring A''] [Semiring B'']
  [Algebra k A''] [Algebra k B''] {P : Type p}
  [AddCommMonoid P] [Module k P] [Module A'' P] [Module B'' P]
  [IsScalarTower k A'' P] [IsScalarTower k B'' P] [SMulCommClass A'' B'' P]

/-- The earned tensor-semilinear maps compose on their original additive functions.
The scalar identification is the native `Algebra.TensorProduct.map_comp` law. -/
theorem ofSemilinearMap_comp (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (ψ : B →ₐ[k] B')
    (φ' : A' →ₐ[k] A'') (ψ' : B' →ₐ[k] B'')
    (f : M →ₗ[k] N) (g : N →ₗ[k] P)
    (hA : ∀ (a : A) (x : M), f (a • x) = φ a • f x)
    (hB : ∀ (b : B) (x : M), f (b • x) = ψ b • f x)
    (hA' : ∀ (a : A') (x : N), g (a • x) = φ' a • g x)
    (hB' : ∀ (b : B') (x : N), g (b • x) = ψ' b • g x) :
    (ofSemilinearMap φ' ψ' g hA' hB').toAddMonoidHom.comp
        (ofSemilinearMap φ ψ f hA hB).toAddMonoidHom =
      (ofSemilinearMap (φ'.comp φ) (ψ'.comp ψ) (g.comp f)
        (fun a x => by
          change g (f (a • x)) = φ' (φ a) • g (f x)
          rw [hA, hA'])
        (fun b x => by
          change g (f (b • x)) = ψ' (ψ b) • g (f x)
          rw [hB, hB'])).toAddMonoidHom := by
  apply AddMonoidHom.ext
  intro x
  rfl

end Composition

end TensorProduct.Algebra

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Pi
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.Projective
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.LinearMap.RetractComparison

/-!
# Tensoring arbitrary products with a finite-projective factor

The product index is arbitrary. Native finite-free tensor coordinates and the
actual finite-free retraction of the tensor factor earn bijectivity of the
original product comparison. No finite product-index hypothesis is used.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe uR uI uN uU uV

variable (R : Type uR) [CommRing R] {ι : Type uI}
  (N : ι → Type uN) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (N i)] [∀ i, Module R (N i)]

attribute [local ext high] TensorProduct.ext

/-- Interchange of the actual finite-free coordinate and original product index. -/
def finitePiFlip (n : ℕ) : (Fin n → ∀ i, N i) ≃ₗ[R] ∀ i, Fin n → N i where
  toFun x i j := x j i
  invFun x j i := x i j
  left_inv _ := rfl
  right_inv _ := rfl
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _ := rfl

/-- The original arbitrary-product tensor comparison respects every actual
linear map in the tensor factor. -/
theorem piRightHom_factor_naturality
    {U : Type uU} {V : Type uV}
    [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U] [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V]
    (f : U →ₗ[R] V) :
    (piRightHom R R V N).comp (f.rTensor (∀ i, N i)) =
      (LinearMap.piMap (fun i => f.rTensor (N i))).comp (piRightHom R R U N) := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro u x
  funext i
  rfl

/-- Native finite-free coordinates compute the original product comparison;
the family and product index remain arbitrary. -/
theorem piRightHom_finiteFree_bijective (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (piRightHom R R (Fin n → R) N) := by
  let eD : (Fin n → R) ⊗[R] (∀ i, N i) ≃ₗ[R] (∀ i, Fin n → N i) :=
    TensorProduct.comm R _ _ ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.piScalarRight R R (∀ i, N i) (Fin n) ≪≫ₗ
      finitePiFlip R N n
  let eC : (∀ i, (Fin n → R) ⊗[R] N i) ≃ₗ[R] (∀ i, Fin n → N i) :=
    LinearEquiv.piCongrRight (fun i => TensorProduct.comm R _ _ ≪≫ₗ
      TensorProduct.piScalarRight R R (N i) (Fin n))
  have he : eC.toLinearMap.comp (piRightHom R R (Fin n → R) N) = eD.toLinearMap := by
    apply TensorProduct.ext'
    intro u x
    funext i j
    change (TensorProduct.piScalarRight R R (N i) (Fin n) (x i ⊗ₜ[R] u)) j =
      (TensorProduct.piScalarRight R R (∀ i, N i) (Fin n) (x ⊗ₜ[R] u)) j i
    simp only [TensorProduct.piScalarRight_apply,
      TensorProduct.piScalarRightHom_tmul, Pi.smul_apply]
  have hb : Function.Bijective (fun x => eC (piRightHom R R (Fin n → R) N x)) := by
    change Function.Bijective (eC.toLinearMap.comp (piRightHom R R (Fin n → R) N))
    rw [he]
    exact eD.bijective
  constructor
  · intro x y h
    exact hb.injective (congrArg eC h)
  · intro y
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hb.surjective (eC y)
    exact ⟨x, eC.injective hx⟩

/-- The actual finite-free projection/inclusion and original comparison squares
earn the finite-projective case through the shared elementary retract provider. -/
theorem piRightHom_finiteFactor_bijective
    (U : Type uU) [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U]
    [Module.Finite R U] [Module.Projective R U] :
    Function.Bijective (piRightHom R R U N) := by
  obtain ⟨n, f, g, hf, hg, hfg⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective R U
  let dF := f.rTensor (∀ i, N i)
  let dG := g.rTensor (∀ i, N i)
  let cF := LinearMap.piMap (fun i => f.rTensor (N i))
  let cG := LinearMap.piMap (fun i => g.rTensor (N i))
  have hd : dF.comp dG = LinearMap.id := by
    rw [← LinearMap.rTensor_comp, hfg, LinearMap.rTensor_id]
  have hc : cF.comp cG = LinearMap.id := by
    ext x i
    have h : (f.rTensor (N i)).comp (g.rTensor (N i)) = LinearMap.id := by
      rw [← LinearMap.rTensor_comp, hfg, LinearMap.rTensor_id]
    exact LinearMap.congr_fun h (x i)
  exact LinearMap.comparison_bijective_of_retract
    (piRightHom R R U N) (piRightHom R R (Fin n → R) N)
    dG dF cG cF hd hc (piRightHom_factor_naturality R N g)
      (piRightHom_factor_naturality R N f) (piRightHom_finiteFree_bijective R N n)

/-- The actual product Iso has the native original product comparison as its
forward map, even for infinite products. -/
def piRightFiniteFactor
    (U : Type uU) [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U]
    [Module.Finite R U] [Module.Projective R U] :
    U ⊗[R] (∀ i, N i) ≃ₗ[R] ∀ i, U ⊗[R] N i :=
  LinearEquiv.ofBijective (piRightHom R R U N) (piRightHom_finiteFactor_bijective R N U)

theorem piRightFiniteFactor_toLinearMap
    (U : Type uU) [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U]
    [Module.Finite R U] [Module.Projective R U] :
    (piRightFiniteFactor R N U).toLinearMap = piRightHom R R U N := rfl

end TensorProduct
