module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.PiFiniteFactor
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.SurjectiveScalarHom

/-!
# Original scalar transport for arbitrary-product tensor comparison

The scalar actions and product functions are the original ones. The native
compatible-scalar tensor coordinates transport the actual finite-projective
factor comparison, preserving every pure tensor and every original projection.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe uR uS uI uN uU

variable {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
  {ι : Type uI} {U : Type uU} [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U] [Module S U]
  [IsScalarTower R S U] (N : ι → Type uN)
  [∀ i, AddCommGroup (N i)] [∀ i, Module R (N i)] [∀ i, Module S (N i)]
  [∀ i, IsScalarTower R S (N i)]

/-- All scalar tensor coordinates and the original finite-factor product map
are constructed internally from the actual surjective scalar action. -/
def piRightFiniteFactorOfSurjectiveScalars
    [Module.Finite S U] [Module.Projective S U]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    U ⊗[R] (∀ i, N i) ≃ₗ[R] ∀ i, U ⊗[R] N i := by
  letI : CompatibleSMul R S U (∀ i, N i) :=
    compatibleSMul_of_surjective_algebraMap (M := U) (J := ∀ i, N i) h
  letI (i : ι) : CompatibleSMul R S U (N i) :=
    compatibleSMul_of_surjective_algebraMap (M := U) (J := N i) h
  exact TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul S R R U (∀ i, N i) ≪≫ₗ
    (piRightFiniteFactor S N U).restrictScalars R ≪≫ₗ
      LinearEquiv.piCongrRight (fun i => TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul R S R U (N i))

/-- Every original pure tensor retains every original product coordinate. -/
theorem piRightFiniteFactorOfSurjectiveScalars_tmul
    [Module.Finite S U] [Module.Projective S U]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) (u : U) (x : ∀ i, N i) (i : ι) :
    piRightFiniteFactorOfSurjectiveScalars N h (u ⊗ₜ[R] x) i = u ⊗ₜ[R] x i := by
  simp [piRightFiniteFactorOfSurjectiveScalars, piRightFiniteFactor,
    TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul, TensorProduct.piRightHom_tmul]

/-- The original R product comparison is the exact forward map. -/
theorem piRightFiniteFactorOfSurjectiveScalars_toLinearMap
    [Module.Finite S U] [Module.Projective S U]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    (piRightFiniteFactorOfSurjectiveScalars N h).toLinearMap = piRightHom R R U N := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro u x
  funext i
  change piRightFiniteFactorOfSurjectiveScalars N h (u ⊗ₜ[R] x) i =
    piRightHom R R U N (u ⊗ₜ[R] x) i
  rw [piRightFiniteFactorOfSurjectiveScalars_tmul, piRightHom_tmul]

end TensorProduct

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.RightExactness
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Quotient.Operations

/-!
# Quotient base change and kernels

For a surjective linear map, base change to a quotient ring is injective
exactly when every element of the original kernel lies in the corresponding
ideal multiple of the source.

The result is stated for arbitrary modules in independent universes.  It
requires no locality, finiteness, freeness, flatness, or smallness assumption.

## Main declaration

* `LinearMap.ker_le_ideal_smul_top_iff_baseChange_quotient_injective`
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open Function
open scoped TensorProduct

universe u v w

namespace LinearMap

/-- For a surjective linear map, quotient base change is injective exactly
when the original kernel is contained in the ideal multiple of the source. -/
theorem ker_le_ideal_smul_top_iff_baseChange_quotient_injective
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    {P : Type v} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (f : P →ₗ[R] M) (hf : Surjective f) :
    LinearMap.ker f ≤ I • (⊤ : Submodule R P) ↔
      Injective (f.baseChange (R ⧸ I)) := by
  constructor
  · intro hker
    have hzeroMap :
        (LinearMap.ker f).subtype.lTensor (R ⧸ I) = 0 := by
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro z
      induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
      | tmul q y =>
          have hyI : (y : P) ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R P) :=
            hker y.property
          simp only [LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, LinearMap.zero_apply]
          obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective q
          have hrone :
              r • (1 : R ⧸ I) = Ideal.Quotient.mk I r := by
            simpa using
              (Submodule.Quotient.mk_smul I r (1 : R)).symm
          rw [← hrone, TensorProduct.smul_tmul]
          change (TensorProduct.mk R (R ⧸ I) P 1)
            (r • (y : P)) = 0
          apply LinearMap.mem_ker.mp
          rw [LinearMap.ker_tensorProductMk]
          exact (I • (⊤ : Submodule R P)).smul_mem r hyI
      | add y z hy hz => simp [hy, hz]
    rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
    intro x hx
    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_lTensor] at hx
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ :=
      ((lTensor_exact (R ⧸ I)
        f.exact_subtype_ker_map hf) x).mp hx
    rw [← hy, hzeroMap, LinearMap.zero_apply]
  · intro hinj x hx
    rw [← LinearMap.ker_tensorProductMk, LinearMap.mem_ker]
    apply hinj
    simp [LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx]

end LinearMap

-- Author: @toskua
module

public import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.IsBaseChangeRightExact
public import Mathlib.Algebra.FiveLemma

/-!
# Right-exact base-change diagrams in tensor coordinates

Apply the stock right-exact four lemma to the actual tensor-base-change
maps. This formulation records the first two comparison equivalences and
the two original commuting squares explicitly.
-/

@[expose] public section
set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
  {U V W U' V' W' : Type*}
  [AddCommGroup U] [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup W]
  [AddCommGroup U'] [AddCommGroup V'] [AddCommGroup W']
  [Module R U] [Module R V] [Module R W]
  [Module S U'] [Module S V'] [Module S W']

/-- Two actual tensor comparison equivalences identify the third map in
a commuting right-exact diagram. -/
theorem baseChange_rightExact_bijective
    (a : U →ₗ[R] V) (q : V →ₗ[R] W) (a' : U' →ₗ[S] V') (q' : V' →ₗ[S] W')
    (v : S ⊗[R] W →ₗ[S] W') (eU : S ⊗[R] U ≃ₗ[S] U') (eV : S ⊗[R] V ≃ₗ[S] V')
    (h₁ : eV.toLinearMap.comp (a.baseChange S) = a'.comp eU.toLinearMap)
    (h₂ : v.comp (q.baseChange S) = q'.comp eV.toLinearMap)
    (hA : Function.Exact a q) (hq : Function.Surjective q)
    (hB : Function.Exact a' q') (hq' : Function.Surjective q') : Function.Bijective v := by
  have hTensor : Function.Exact (a.baseChange S) (q.baseChange S) := by
    simpa only [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_lTensor] using _root_.lTensor_exact S hA hq
  exact LinearMap.bijective_of_surjective_of_bijective_of_right_exact
    (a.baseChange S) (q.baseChange S) a' q' eU.toLinearMap eV.toLinearMap v
    h₁.symm h₂.symm hTensor hB eU.surjective eV.bijective
    (q.baseChange_surjective S hq) hq'

end LinearMap

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Contraction
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Tower

/-!
# Actual finite tensor–Hom transport along a surjective scalar map

Native scalar extension identifies the original linear maps, and native
compatible-scalar tensor equivalences retain every original pure tensor.
The only finite-projective contraction is the existing native equivalence.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe uR uS uM uJ uU

variable {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
  {M : Type uM} {J : Type uJ} {U : Type uU}
  [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup J] [AddCommGroup U]
  [Module R M] [Module R J] [Module R U]
  [Module S M] [Module S J] [Module S U]
  [IsScalarTower R S M] [IsScalarTower R S J] [IsScalarTower R S U]

/-- A surjective actual scalar map proves compatibility on the original R tensor. -/
theorem compatibleSMul_of_surjective_algebraMap
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) : CompatibleSMul R S M J where
  smul_tmul s m j := by
    obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := h s
    simpa only [algebraMap_smul] using (TensorProduct.smul_tmul (R := R) r m j)

/-- Original scalar/input tensor coordinates; no finite-projectivity premise is used. -/
def rTensorHomScalarInputEquiv
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    (M →ₗ[R] J) ⊗[R] U ≃ₗ[R] (M →ₗ[S] J) ⊗[S] U := by
  letI : CompatibleSMul R S (M →ₗ[S] J) U :=
    compatibleSMul_of_surjective_algebraMap (M := M →ₗ[S] J) (J := U) h
  let eHom : (M →ₗ[R] J) ≃ₗ[R] M →ₗ[S] J :=
    LinearMap.extendScalarsOfSurjectiveEquiv h
  exact TensorProduct.congr eHom (LinearEquiv.refl R U) ≪≫ₗ
    TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul S R R (M →ₗ[S] J) U

/-- Original scalar/output Hom coordinates, retaining every original underlying function. -/
def rTensorHomScalarOutputEquiv
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    (M →ₗ[S] J ⊗[S] U) ≃ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] J ⊗[R] U := by
  letI : CompatibleSMul R S J U :=
    compatibleSMul_of_surjective_algebraMap (M := J) (J := U) h
  let eTensor : J ⊗[S] U ≃ₗ[R] J ⊗[R] U :=
    TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul R S R J U
  exact (LinearMap.extendScalarsOfSurjectiveEquiv
    (R := R) (S := S) (M := M) (N := J ⊗[S] U) h).symm ≪≫ₗ
      (LinearEquiv.refl R M).arrowCongr eTensor

/-- The actual native coefficient transports followed by the existing S contraction.
The original construction is factored through the same unchanged scalar coordinates. -/
def rTensorHomEquivOfSurjectiveScalars
    [Module.Projective S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    (M →ₗ[R] J) ⊗[R] U ≃ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] J ⊗[R] U :=
  rTensorHomScalarInputEquiv h ≪≫ₗ
    (_root_.rTensorHomEquivHomRTensor S M J U).restrictScalars R ≪≫ₗ
      rTensorHomScalarOutputEquiv h

/-- The transport retains the canonical original R-linear evaluation on every pure tensor. -/
theorem rTensorHomEquivOfSurjectiveScalars_tmul
    [Module.Projective S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) (f : M →ₗ[R] J) (u : U) (m : M) :
    rTensorHomEquivOfSurjectiveScalars (M := M) (J := J) (U := U) h (f ⊗ₜ[R] u) m =
      f m ⊗ₜ[R] u := by
  simp [rTensorHomEquivOfSurjectiveScalars, rTensorHomScalarInputEquiv,
    rTensorHomScalarOutputEquiv, TensorProduct.congr_tmul,
    _root_.rTensorHomEquivHomRTensor_apply, TensorProduct.rTensorHomToHomRTensor_apply,
    TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul, LinearEquiv.arrowCongr,
    LinearMap.extendScalarsOfSurjectiveEquiv]

/-- The forward linear map is the exact original R coefficient map, independent of
the quotient/transport used to earn its inverse. -/
theorem rTensorHomEquivOfSurjectiveScalars_toLinearMap
    [Module.Projective S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R S)) :
    (rTensorHomEquivOfSurjectiveScalars (M := M) (J := J) (U := U) h).toLinearMap =
      TensorProduct.rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) M J U := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro f u
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro m
  change rTensorHomEquivOfSurjectiveScalars (M := M) (J := J) (U := U) h
      (f ⊗ₜ[R] u) m = TensorProduct.rTensorHomToHomRTensor (.id R) M J U (f ⊗ₜ[R] u) m
  rw [rTensorHomEquivOfSurjectiveScalars_tmul, TensorProduct.rTensorHomToHomRTensor_apply]

end TensorProduct

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.DirectedSystem

/-!
# Tensor products of two directed module systems

If a tensor from two directed systems vanishes after mapping both factors to
their direct limits, it vanishes after one common later transition.
The historical constructors below are compatibility abbreviations of the
generalized `Diagonal` API; they do not define another colimit or inverse.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

open Module Module.DirectLimit

namespace TensorProduct

variable {R ι : Type*} [CommRing R] [DecidableEq ι]
variable [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι]
section Vanishing
variable {G H : ι → Type*}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] [∀ i, Module R (G i)]
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, Module R (H i)]
variable (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[R] G j)
variable (g : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → H i →ₗ[R] H j)
variable [DirectedSystem G (f · · ·)] [DirectedSystem H (g · · ·)]

/-- Vanishing after mapping two stagewise factors to their direct limits is
detected after one common enlargement. -/
theorem exists_eq_zero_of_map_to_two_directLimits_tensor_eq_zero
    {i : ι} (x : G i ⊗[R] H i)
    (hx : TensorProduct.map
      (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i)
      (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι H g i) x = 0) :
    ∃ j : ι, ∃ hij : i ≤ j,
      TensorProduct.map (f i j hij) (g i j hij) x = 0 := by
  exact exists_eq_zero_of_map_to_directLimit_diagonal_eq_zero f g x hx

end Vanishing

variable {G : ι → Type*}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] [∀ i, Module R (G i)]
variable (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[R] G j)
variable [DirectedSystem G (f · · ·)]

/-- The diagonal tensor-product transition attached to two directed module
systems. -/
noncomputable abbrev directedTensorTransition
    {H : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, Module R (H i)]
    (g : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → H i →ₗ[R] H j)
    (i j : ι) (hij : i ≤ j) :
    G i ⊗[R] H i →ₗ[R] G j ⊗[R] H j :=
  diagonalTransition f g i j hij

/-- Tensoring two directed systems stagewise again gives a directed
system. -/
instance directedTensorSystem
    {H : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, Module R (H i)]
    (g : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → H i →ₗ[R] H j)
    [DirectedSystem H (g · · ·)] :
    DirectedSystem (fun i => G i ⊗[R] H i)
      (directedTensorTransition f g · · ·) :=
  diagonalDirectedSystem f g

/-- The canonical map from the direct limit of the stagewise tensor
products to the tensor product of the two direct limits. -/
noncomputable abbrev diagonalDirectLimitToTensor
    {H : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, Module R (H i)]
    (g : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → H i →ₗ[R] H j)
    : Module.DirectLimit (fun i => G i ⊗[R] H i)
        (directedTensorTransition f g) →ₗ[R]
      Module.DirectLimit G f ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit H g :=
  diagonalToTensor f g

omit [IsDirectedOrder ι] [DirectedSystem G (f · · ·)] in
theorem diagonalDirectLimitToTensor_of
    {H : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, Module R (H i)]
    (g : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → H i →ₗ[R] H j)
    (i : ι) (x : G i ⊗[R] H i) :
    diagonalDirectLimitToTensor f g
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _ (directedTensorTransition f g) i x) =
      TensorProduct.map
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i)
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι H g i) x := by
  exact diagonalToTensor_of f g i x

/-- The canonical diagonal direct-limit map is bijective.  Thus filtered
direct limits commute with a stagewise binary tensor product even when both
factors vary over the same directed index. -/
theorem diagonalDirectLimitToTensor_bijective
    {H : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, Module R (H i)]
    (g : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → H i →ₗ[R] H j)
    [DirectedSystem H (g · · ·)] :
    Function.Bijective (diagonalDirectLimitToTensor f g) := by
  exact (directLimitDiagonal f g).bijective

/-- The direct limit of the stagewise tensor products is canonically
linearly equivalent to the tensor product of the two direct limits. -/
noncomputable abbrev diagonalDirectLimitEquivTensor
    {H : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, Module R (H i)]
    (g : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → H i →ₗ[R] H j)
    [DirectedSystem H (g · · ·)] :
    Module.DirectLimit (fun i => G i ⊗[R] H i)
        (directedTensorTransition f g) ≃ₗ[R]
      Module.DirectLimit G f ⊗[R] Module.DirectLimit H g :=
  directLimitDiagonal f g

theorem diagonalDirectLimitEquivTensor_apply_of
    {H : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, Module R (H i)]
    (g : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → H i →ₗ[R] H j)
    [DirectedSystem H (g · · ·)]
    (i : ι) (x : G i ⊗[R] H i) :
    diagonalDirectLimitEquivTensor f g
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι _ (directedTensorTransition f g) i x) =
      TensorProduct.map
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι G f i)
        (Module.DirectLimit.of R ι H g i) x :=
  directLimitDiagonal_of f g i x


end TensorProduct

-- Author: @toskua
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.ZMod
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Basic

/-!
# Tensor products after restricting `ZMod n`-modules to `ℤ`

For `ZMod n`-modules `M` and `N`, the tensor product of their underlying
abelian groups over `ℤ` is canonically isomorphic to `M ⊗[ZMod n] N` after
forgetting its scalar structure to `ℤ`.  The construction uses only the
universal properties and the fact that the integral tensor product is
`n`-torsion.

The canonical equivalence accepts the actual stored integer module
structures. Their equality with the canonical integer action is the stock
uniqueness theorem, so this extension retains the same tensor comparison.

The statement includes `n = 0`, where `ZMod 0 = ℤ`.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u v

namespace TensorProduct

variable (n : ℕ) (M : Type u) (N : Type v)
variable [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
variable [Module (ZMod n) M] [Module (ZMod n) N]

omit [Module (ZMod n) N] in
/-- The integral tensor product of two `ZMod n`-modules is `n`-torsion. -/
theorem intTensor_nsmul_eq_zero (z : TensorProduct ℤ M N) : n • z = 0 := by
  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul x y =>
      rw [← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℤ, TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
      rw [Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul]
      rw [ZModModule.char_nsmul_eq_zero, zero_tmul]
  | add x y hx hy =>
      rw [nsmul_add, hx, hy, add_zero]

/-- Canonical integral-linear map from the tensor product over `ℤ` to the
tensor product over `ZMod n`. -/
noncomputable def intToZMod :
    TensorProduct ℤ M N →ₗ[ℤ] TensorProduct (ZMod n) M N := by
  let inner (x : M) : N →+ TensorProduct (ZMod n) M N :=
    { toFun := fun y => x ⊗ₜ[ZMod n] y
      map_zero' := by simp
      map_add' := by intro y z; rw [tmul_add] }
  let outer : M →+ (N →ₗ[ℤ] TensorProduct (ZMod n) M N) :=
    { toFun := fun x => (inner x).toIntLinearMap
      map_zero' := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro y
        simp [inner]
      map_add' := fun x y => by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro z
        simp [inner, add_tmul] }
  exact TensorProduct.lift outer.toIntLinearMap

@[simp]
theorem intToZMod_tmul (x : M) (y : N) :
    intToZMod n M N (x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y) = x ⊗ₜ[ZMod n] y :=
  rfl

/-- Canonical `ZMod n`-linear map back to the integral tensor product,
equipped with its canonical `n`-torsion module structure. -/
noncomputable def zmodToInt :
    TensorProduct (ZMod n) M N →ₗ[ZMod n] TensorProduct ℤ M N := by
  let inner (x : M) : N →+ TensorProduct ℤ M N :=
    { toFun := fun y => x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y
      map_zero' := by simp
      map_add' := by intro y z; rw [tmul_add] }
  let outer : M →+ (N →ₗ[ZMod n] TensorProduct ℤ M N) :=
    { toFun := fun x => (inner x).toZModLinearMap n
      map_zero' := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro y
        simp [inner]
      map_add' := fun x y => by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro z
        simp [inner, add_tmul] }
  exact TensorProduct.lift (outer.toZModLinearMap n)

@[simp]
theorem zmodToInt_tmul (x : M) (y : N) :
    zmodToInt n M N (x ⊗ₜ[ZMod n] y) = x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y :=
  by simp [zmodToInt]

/-- The `ℤ`-linear form of `zmodToInt`, forgetting its `ZMod n` scalar
structure. -/
noncomputable def zmodToIntLinear :
    TensorProduct (ZMod n) M N →ₗ[ℤ] TensorProduct ℤ M N :=
  (zmodToInt n M N).toAddMonoidHom.toIntLinearMap

@[simp]
theorem zmodToIntLinear_tmul (x : M) (y : N) :
    zmodToIntLinear n M N (x ⊗ₜ[ZMod n] y) = x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y := by
  change zmodToInt n M N (x ⊗ₜ[ZMod n] y) = _
  rw [zmodToInt_tmul]

variable [iM : Module ℤ M] [iN : Module ℤ N]

/-- Canonical comparison between tensoring two `ZMod n`-modules over `ℤ`
and tensoring them over `ZMod n`, with the latter restricted to `ℤ`. -/
noncomputable def zmodRestrictIntEquiv :
    TensorProduct ℤ M N ≃ₗ[ℤ] TensorProduct (ZMod n) M N := by
  cases Subsingleton.elim iM (AddCommGroup.toIntModule (M := M))
  cases Subsingleton.elim iN (AddCommGroup.toIntModule (M := N))
  exact {
    __ := intToZMod n M N
    invFun := zmodToIntLinear n M N
    left_inv z := by
      induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
      | tmul x y =>
          change zmodToIntLinear n M N
            (intToZMod n M N (x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y)) = _
          rw [intToZMod_tmul, zmodToIntLinear_tmul]
      | add x y hx hy =>
          change zmodToIntLinear n M N
            (intToZMod n M N (x + y)) = _
          rw [map_add, map_add]
          exact congrArg₂ (fun a b => a + b) hx hy
    right_inv z := by
      induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
      | tmul x y =>
          change intToZMod n M N
            (zmodToIntLinear n M N (x ⊗ₜ[ZMod n] y)) = _
          rw [zmodToIntLinear_tmul, intToZMod_tmul]
      | add x y hx hy =>
          change intToZMod n M N
            (zmodToIntLinear n M N (x + y)) = _
          rw [map_add, map_add]
          exact congrArg₂ (fun a b => a + b) hx hy }

@[simp]
theorem zmodRestrictIntEquiv_apply_tmul (x : M) (y : N) :
    zmodRestrictIntEquiv n M N (x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y) =
      x ⊗ₜ[ZMod n] y :=
  by
    cases Subsingleton.elim iM (AddCommGroup.toIntModule (M := M))
    cases Subsingleton.elim iN (AddCommGroup.toIntModule (M := N))
    rfl

@[simp]
theorem zmodRestrictIntEquiv_symm_apply_tmul (x : M) (y : N) :
    (zmodRestrictIntEquiv n M N).symm (x ⊗ₜ[ZMod n] y) =
      x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y :=
  by
    cases Subsingleton.elim iM (AddCommGroup.toIntModule (M := M))
    cases Subsingleton.elim iN (AddCommGroup.toIntModule (M := N))
    exact zmodToIntLinear_tmul n M N x y

end TensorProduct

  Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.ZModRestrict
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Map

/-!
# Naturality of the `ℤ`/`ZMod n` tensor comparison

The canonical equivalence from tensoring two `ZMod n` modules over `ℤ`
to tensoring them over `ZMod n` is natural in a pair of `ZMod n`-linear
maps.  The statement is made over `ℤ` after forgetting the scalar
structure on the target tensor product.

The result includes `n = 0`.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace TensorProduct

universe u v u' v'

variable (n : ℕ)
variable {M : Type u} {N : Type v} {M' : Type u'} {N' : Type v'}
variable [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
variable [AddCommGroup M'] [AddCommGroup N']
variable [Module (ZMod n) M] [Module (ZMod n) N]
variable [Module (ZMod n) M'] [Module (ZMod n) N']

/-- Naturality of `zmodRestrictIntEquiv` under a pair of `ZMod n`-linear
maps. -/
theorem zmodRestrictIntEquiv_naturality
    (f : M →ₗ[ZMod n] M') (g : N →ₗ[ZMod n] N') :
    (TensorProduct.map f g).toAddMonoidHom.toIntLinearMap.comp
        (zmodRestrictIntEquiv n M N).toLinearMap =
      (zmodRestrictIntEquiv n M' N').toLinearMap.comp
        (TensorProduct.map
          f.toAddMonoidHom.toIntLinearMap
          g.toAddMonoidHom.toIntLinearMap) := by
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro x y
  rfl

end TensorProduct

/-
  Author: @toskua, Avocado
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Sum

/-!
# Two-point complement equivalence

This file constructs an equivalence between `Fin 2 ⊕ {x // x ≠ a ∧ x ≠ b}`
and `α` for distinct points `a b : α`. The left summand maps `0` to `a`
and `1` to `b`, and the right summand maps a complement element to its
underlying value. The construction uses only decidable equality and avoids
any finiteness or cardinality assumptions.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Equiv

variable {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]

/-- Equivalence isolating two distinct points `a` and `b`. -/
def twoPointSumCompl (a b : α) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    Fin 2 ⊕ {x : α // x ≠ a ∧ x ≠ b} ≃ α where
  toFun
    | Sum.inl 0 => a
    | Sum.inl 1 => b
    | Sum.inr x => x.val
  invFun y :=
    if hya : y = a then Sum.inl 0
    else if hyb : y = b then Sum.inl 1
    else Sum.inr ⟨y, hya, hyb⟩
  left_inv := by
    intro s
    match s with
    | Sum.inl 0 =>
      simp
    | Sum.inl 1 =>
      simp [Ne.symm hab]
    | Sum.inr x =>
      have h1 : (x : α) ≠ a := x.2.1
      have h2 : (x : α) ≠ b := x.2.2
      simp [h1, h2]
  right_inv := by
    intro y
    by_cases hya : y = a
    · subst hya
      simp
    · by_cases hyb : y = b
      · subst hyb
        simp [Ne.symm hab]
      · simp [hya, hyb]

@[simp]
theorem twoPointSumCompl_symm_apply_first (a b : α) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    (twoPointSumCompl a b hab).symm a = Sum.inl (0 : Fin 2) := by
  simp [twoPointSumCompl]

@[simp]
theorem twoPointSumCompl_symm_apply_second (a b : α) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    (twoPointSumCompl a b hab).symm b = Sum.inl (1 : Fin 2) := by
  simp [twoPointSumCompl, Ne.symm hab]

@[simp]
theorem twoPointSumCompl_symm_apply_other (a b : α) (hab : a ≠ b)
    (x : α) (hxa : x ≠ a) (hxb : x ≠ b) :
    (twoPointSumCompl a b hab).symm x = Sum.inr ⟨x, hxa, hxb⟩ := by
  simp [twoPointSumCompl, hxa, hxb]

end Equiv

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.lpSpace
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Complex
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.SimpleFuncDense

import Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.ProperSpace

/-!
# Bounded measurable functions with the pointwise supremum norm

This file defines the bounded measurable complex-valued functions on a measurable space as the
closed star subalgebra of the raw bounded-function space `lp (fun _ => ℂ) ∞`.  Thus equality is
pointwise equality, not almost-everywhere equality, and all normed algebra and C-star structure is
inherited from the canonical `lp` carrier.

The API includes measurable indicators, conversion of measurable simple functions, and uniform
approximation by finite-range measurable functions.  No measure on the source type is required.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter MeasureTheory Set TopologicalSpace
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology

namespace MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function

noncomputable section

universe u

variable (X : Type u) [MeasurableSpace X]

/-- The star subalgebra of raw bounded functions consisting of the measurable functions. -/
noncomputable def boundedMeasurableFunctions :
    StarSubalgebra ℂ (lp (fun _ : X ↦ ℂ) ∞) where
  carrier := {f | Measurable fun x ↦ f x}
  zero_mem' := by
    change Measurable fun _ : X ↦ (0 : ℂ)
    exact measurable_const
  add_mem' := by
    intro f g hf hg
    change Measurable fun x ↦ f x + g x
    exact hf.add hg
  mul_mem' := by
    intro f g hf hg
    change Measurable fun x ↦ f x * g x
    exact hf.mul hg
  one_mem' := by
    change Measurable fun _ : X ↦ (1 : ℂ)
    exact measurable_const
  algebraMap_mem' := by
    intro c
    change Measurable fun _ : X ↦ c
    exact measurable_const
  star_mem' := by
    intro f hf
    change Measurable fun x ↦ star (f x)
    exact Complex.continuous_conj.measurable.comp hf

/-- Bounded measurable complex-valued functions, with pointwise equality and the supremum norm. -/
abbrev BoundedMeasurableFunction := ↥(boundedMeasurableFunctions X)

namespace BoundedMeasurableFunction

variable {X}

instance : CoeFun (BoundedMeasurableFunction X) (fun _ ↦ X → ℂ) where
  coe f := f.1

/-- The underlying raw bounded function of a bounded measurable function. -/
abbrev toLp (f : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) : lp (fun _ : X ↦ ℂ) ∞ := f

/-- Coercing to the raw bounded function preserves the original pointwise function. -/
theorem coe_toLp (f : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    (f.toLp : X → ℂ) = f :=
  rfl

/-- Build a bounded measurable function from its actual raw function and pointwise norm bound.
No nonempty source or nonnegative bound is required by the DATA constructor. -/
noncomputable def ofBound (f : X → ℂ) (hf : Measurable f) (C : ℝ)
    (hC : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) : BoundedMeasurableFunction X := by
  classical
  exact ⟨⟨(show PreLp (fun _ : X => ℂ) from f), by
    change Memℓp f ∞
    rw [memℓp_infty_iff]
    refine ⟨C, ?_⟩
    rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
    exact hC x⟩, hf⟩

/-- Evaluation of the actual bound-based constructor is the original pointwise function. -/
@[simp]
theorem ofBound_apply (f : X → ℂ) (hf : Measurable f) (C : ℝ)
    (hC : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (x : X) : ofBound f hf C hC x = f x := rfl

/-- The constructor retains its original pointwise norm bound. -/
theorem norm_ofBound_apply_le (f : X → ℂ) (hf : Measurable f) (C : ℝ)
    (hC : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (x : X) : ‖ofBound f hf C hC x‖ ≤ C := hC x

/-- A nonnegative pointwise bound controls the supremum norm, including on the empty source. -/
theorem norm_ofBound_le (f : X → ℂ) (hf : Measurable f) (C : ℝ)
    (hC : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (hC0 : 0 ≤ C) : ‖ofBound f hf C hC‖ ≤ C := by
  change ‖(ofBound f hf C hC).toLp‖ ≤ C
  exact lp.norm_le_of_forall_le hC0 hC

/-- The supremum norm has a uniform bound without imposing nonemptiness or a bound sign. -/
theorem norm_ofBound_le_max (f : X → ℂ) (hf : Measurable f) (C : ℝ)
    (hC : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) : ‖ofBound f hf C hC‖ ≤ max C 0 := by
  change ‖(ofBound f hf C hC).toLp‖ ≤ max C 0
  exact lp.norm_le_of_forall_le (le_max_right C 0)
    (fun x => (hC x).trans (le_max_left C 0))

/-- A bounded measurable function is measurable as an ordinary pointwise function. -/
theorem measurable (f : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) : Measurable fun x ↦ f x :=
  show Measurable (fun x ↦ f.1 x) from f.property

/-- The norm is the pointwise supremum norm, including on the empty source type. -/
theorem norm_eq_iSup_norm (f : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    ‖f‖ = ⨆ x : X, ‖f x‖ :=
  lp.norm_eq_ciSup f.toLp

/-- Evaluation at every point is bounded by the supremum norm. -/
theorem norm_apply_le_norm (f : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) (x : X) :
    ‖f x‖ ≤ ‖f‖ :=
  lp.norm_apply_le_norm ENNReal.top_ne_zero f.toLp x

end BoundedMeasurableFunction

/-- The measurable bounded-function star subalgebra is closed in the raw supremum-norm space. -/
theorem isClosed_boundedMeasurableFunctions :
    IsClosed (boundedMeasurableFunctions X : Set (lp (fun _ : X ↦ ℂ) ∞)) := by
  rw [← isSeqClosed_iff_isClosed]
  intro f g hf hfg
  change Measurable fun x ↦ g x
  apply measurable_of_tendsto_metrizable (fun n ↦ show Measurable (fun x ↦ f n x) from hf n)
  rw [tendsto_pi_nhds]
  intro x
  exact ((lp.evalCLM ℂ (fun _ : X ↦ ℂ) ∞ x).continuous.tendsto _).comp hfg

noncomputable instance boundedMeasurableFunctionsIsClosed :
    IsClosed (boundedMeasurableFunctions X : Set (lp (fun _ : X ↦ ℂ) ∞)) :=
  isClosed_boundedMeasurableFunctions X

namespace BoundedMeasurableFunction

variable {X}

/-! ### Measurable simple functions and indicators -/

/-- A measurable simple function, regarded as a bounded measurable function. -/
noncomputable def ofSimpleFunc (f : SimpleFunc X ℂ) : BoundedMeasurableFunction X :=
  by
    classical
    exact
      ⟨⟨(show PreLp (fun _ : X ↦ ℂ) from fun x ↦ f x), by
          change Memℓp (fun x ↦ f x) ∞
          rw [memℓp_infty_iff]
          refine ⟨∑ y ∈ f.range, ‖y‖, ?_⟩
          rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
          exact Finset.single_le_sum (fun y _ ↦ norm_nonneg y) (f.mem_range_self x)⟩,
        f.measurable⟩

@[simp]
theorem ofSimpleFunc_apply (f : SimpleFunc X ℂ) (x : X) : ofSimpleFunc f x = f x :=
  rfl

/-- A measurable-set indicator with the constant value `c` on the set. -/
noncomputable def indicatorConst (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (c : ℂ) :
    BoundedMeasurableFunction X :=
  ofSimpleFunc <| SimpleFunc.piecewise s hs (SimpleFunc.const X c) 0

@[simp]
theorem indicatorConst_apply (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (c : ℂ) (x : X) :
    indicatorConst s hs c x = s.indicator (fun _ ↦ c) x := by
  by_cases hx : x ∈ s <;> simp [indicatorConst, hx]

/-- The characteristic function of a measurable set as a bounded measurable function. -/
noncomputable def indicator (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    BoundedMeasurableFunction X :=
  indicatorConst s hs 1

@[simp]
theorem indicator_apply (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (x : X) :
    indicator s hs x = s.indicator (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℂ)) x := by
  rw [indicator, indicatorConst_apply]

@[simp]
theorem indicatorConst_empty (c : ℂ) :
    indicatorConst (∅ : Set X) MeasurableSet.empty c = 0 := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  apply lp.ext
  funext x
  simp

@[simp]
theorem indicator_empty : indicator (∅ : Set X) MeasurableSet.empty = 0 := by
  simp [indicator]

@[simp]
theorem indicator_univ : indicator (Set.univ : Set X) MeasurableSet.univ = 1 := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  apply lp.ext
  funext x
  simp

@[simp]
theorem indicator_inter (s t : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (ht : MeasurableSet t) :
    indicator (s ∩ t) (hs.inter ht) = indicator s hs * indicator t ht := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  apply lp.ext
  funext x
  by_cases hxs : x ∈ s <;> by_cases hxt : x ∈ t <;> simp [indicator_apply, hxs, hxt]

@[simp]
theorem star_indicator (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    star (indicator s hs) = indicator s hs := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  apply lp.ext
  funext x
  by_cases hx : x ∈ s <;> simp [indicator_apply, hx]

/-- The norm of a constant-valued indicator is at most the norm of its value. -/
theorem norm_indicatorConst_le (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (c : ℂ) :
    ‖indicatorConst s hs c‖ ≤ ‖c‖ := by
  change ‖(indicatorConst s hs c).toLp‖ ≤ ‖c‖
  apply lp.norm_le_of_forall_le (norm_nonneg c)
  intro x
  by_cases hx : x ∈ s <;> simp [indicatorConst_apply, hx]

/-- On a nonempty set, a constant-valued indicator has exactly the norm of its value. -/
theorem norm_indicatorConst (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hne : s.Nonempty) (c : ℂ) :
    ‖indicatorConst s hs c‖ = ‖c‖ := by
  apply le_antisymm (norm_indicatorConst_le s hs c)
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hne
  calc
    ‖c‖ = ‖indicatorConst s hs c x‖ := by simp [indicatorConst_apply, hx]
    _ ≤ ‖indicatorConst s hs c‖ := norm_apply_le_norm _ _

/-- A nonempty measurable set has characteristic function of norm one. -/
theorem norm_indicator (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hne : s.Nonempty) :
    ‖indicator s hs‖ = 1 := by
  simpa [indicator] using norm_indicatorConst s hs hne (1 : ℂ)

/-! ### Uniform finite-range approximation -/

private theorem exists_simpleFunc_uniform_approx
    (f : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    ∃ g : SimpleFunc X ℂ, ∀ x, dist (g x) (f x) < r := by
  classical
  let K : Set ℂ := Metric.closedBall 0 ‖f‖
  have hK : IsCompact K := isCompact_closedBall 0 ‖f‖
  let : Nonempty K := ⟨⟨0, by simp [K]⟩⟩
  let e : ℕ → ℂ := fun n ↦ (denseSeq K n : ℂ)
  have hcover : K ⊆ ⋃ n : ℕ, Metric.ball (e n) r := by
    intro y hy
    obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := Metric.denseRange_iff.mp (denseRange_denseSeq K) ⟨y, hy⟩ r hr
    have hn' : dist y (e n) < r := by
      simpa only [e, Subtype.dist_eq] using hn
    refine Set.mem_iUnion.2 ⟨n, ?_⟩
    simpa [Metric.mem_ball] using hn'
  obtain ⟨t, _htuniv, htfinite, htcover⟩ :=
    hK.elim_finite_subcover_image (b := Set.univ)
      (c := fun n : ℕ ↦ Metric.ball (e n) r)
      (fun _ _ ↦ Metric.isOpen_ball) (by simpa using hcover)
  have htne : t.Nonempty := by
    have hzero : (0 : ℂ) ∈ K := by simp [K]
    obtain ⟨n, hnt, _hn⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp (htcover hzero)
    exact ⟨n, hnt⟩
  let u : Finset ℕ := htfinite.toFinset
  have hune : u.Nonempty := by
    simpa [u] using htne
  let N : ℕ := u.max' hune
  let q : SimpleFunc ℂ ℂ := SimpleFunc.nearestPt e N
  let g : SimpleFunc X ℂ := q.comp (fun x ↦ f x) f.measurable
  refine ⟨g, fun x ↦ ?_⟩
  have hfxK : f x ∈ K := by
    change dist (f x) 0 ≤ ‖f‖
    rw [dist_zero_right]
    exact f.norm_apply_le_norm x
  obtain ⟨n, hnt, hball⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp (htcover hfxK)
  have hnu : n ∈ u := by
    simpa [u] using hnt
  have hnN : n ≤ N := by
    dsimp only [N]
    simpa using Finset.le_max' u n hnu
  have hnear := SimpleFunc.edist_nearestPt_le e (f x) hnN
  have hnear' : dist (q (f x)) (f x) ≤ dist (e n) (f x) := by
    simpa [q, edist_dist] using hnear
  have hball' : dist (e n) (f x) < r := by
    simpa [Metric.mem_ball, dist_comm] using hball
  change dist (q (f x)) (f x) < r
  exact hnear'.trans_lt hball'

/-- Every bounded measurable function is uniformly approximable by measurable simple functions. -/
theorem exists_simpleFunc_norm_sub_lt
    (f : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    ∃ g : SimpleFunc X ℂ, ‖f - ofSimpleFunc g‖ < r := by
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := exists_simpleFunc_uniform_approx f (half_pos hr)
  have hle : ‖(f - ofSimpleFunc g).toLp‖ ≤ r / 2 := by
    apply lp.norm_le_of_forall_le (half_pos hr).le
    intro x
    change ‖f x - ofSimpleFunc g x‖ ≤ r / 2
    simpa only [ofSimpleFunc_apply, dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_rev] using (hg x).le
  exact ⟨g, hle.trans_lt (half_lt_self hr)⟩

/-- Every bounded measurable function is uniformly approximable by finite-range bounded measurable
functions. -/
theorem exists_finiteRange_norm_sub_lt
    (f : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    ∃ g : BoundedMeasurableFunction X,
      (Set.range fun x ↦ g x).Finite ∧ ‖f - g‖ < r := by
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := exists_simpleFunc_norm_sub_lt f hr
  refine ⟨ofSimpleFunc g, ?_, hg⟩
  have hfun : (fun x ↦ ofSimpleFunc g x) = fun x ↦ g x := by
    funext x
    exact ofSimpleFunc_apply g x
  rw [hfun]
  exact g.finite_range

end BoundedMeasurableFunction

end

end MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function

module

public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function.BoundedMeasurable
public import Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.Compact

/-!
# Continuous functions as bounded measurable functions

On a compact Borel space, every complex-valued continuous function
is bounded and measurable.  This file packages the pointwise inclusion

`C(X, ℂ) →⋆ₐ[ℂ] BoundedMeasurableFunction X`

and proves that it is isometric.  The construction also covers the empty
compact space and installs no new instances.
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory TopologicalSpace
open scoped ENNReal NNReal

namespace MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function
namespace BoundedMeasurableFunction

noncomputable section

universe u

variable {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [CompactSpace X]
variable [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]

/-- A continuous complex-valued function on a compact Borel space, regarded
as a bounded measurable function. -/
noncomputable def ofContinuousMap (f : C(X, ℂ)) : BoundedMeasurableFunction X :=
  ⟨⟨(show PreLp (fun _ : X ↦ ℂ) from fun x ↦ f x), by
      change Memℓp (fun x ↦ f x) ∞
      rw [memℓp_infty_iff]
      refine ⟨‖f‖, ?_⟩
      rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
      exact f.norm_coe_le_norm x⟩,
    f.continuous.measurable⟩

@[simp]
theorem ofContinuousMap_apply (f : C(X, ℂ)) (x : X) :
    ofContinuousMap f x = f x :=
  rfl

/-- The continuous-function inclusion, bundled as a unital complex
star-algebra homomorphism. -/
noncomputable def continuousMapStarAlgHom :
    C(X, ℂ) →⋆ₐ[ℂ] BoundedMeasurableFunction X where
  toFun := ofContinuousMap
  map_one' := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply lp.ext
    funext x
    rfl
  map_mul' f g := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply lp.ext
    funext x
    rfl
  map_zero' := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply lp.ext
    funext x
    rfl
  map_add' f g := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply lp.ext
    funext x
    rfl
  commutes' c := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply lp.ext
    funext x
    rfl
  map_star' f := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply lp.ext
    funext x
    rfl

@[simp]
theorem continuousMapStarAlgHom_apply (f : C(X, ℂ)) (x : X) :
    continuousMapStarAlgHom f x = f x :=
  rfl

theorem continuousMapStarAlgHom_measurable (f : C(X, ℂ)) :
    Measurable fun x ↦ continuousMapStarAlgHom f x :=
  (continuousMapStarAlgHom f).measurable

/-- The inclusion preserves the compact sup norm, including when `X` is
empty. -/
@[simp]
theorem norm_continuousMapStarAlgHom (f : C(X, ℂ)) :
    ‖continuousMapStarAlgHom f‖ = ‖f‖ := by
  rw [BoundedMeasurableFunction.norm_eq_iSup_norm,
    ContinuousMap.norm_eq_iSup_norm]
  rfl

theorem isometry_continuousMapStarAlgHom :
    Isometry (continuousMapStarAlgHom (X := X)) :=
  AddMonoidHomClass.isometry_of_norm (continuousMapStarAlgHom (X := X))
    (norm_continuousMapStarAlgHom (X := X))

end

end BoundedMeasurableFunction
end MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function

module

public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ConvergenceInMeasure
public import Mathlib.Topology.Instances.ENNReal.Lemmas

/-!
# Actual bounded continuous indicator approximation in L2 and almost everywhere

These strict approximation facts serve the actual CFC coefficient-operator
intersection/projection construction, hence resolutionOfIdentity and BFC DATA.
The original measurable set and finite weakly regular measure are inputs.
No PVM, projection, norm bound, field or desired-output certificate is assumed.
Stock continuous Lp density gives approximants; actual max/min clipping keeps
their values in[0,1] and does not increase indicator error. A stock convergence-
in-measure subsequence preserves L2 convergence and gives a.e. convergence.
The normal-space hypotheses hold for every compact metric spectrum; no new
restriction on the original Hilbert space or a nonempty spectrum is introduced.
-/

@[expose] public section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Filter Set
open scoped Topology ENNReal
namespace MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function
universe uX
variable {X : Type uX} [TopologicalSpace X] [NormalSpace X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]

private theorem clip_norm_sub_zero (t : ℝ) :
    ‖max 0 (min 1 t) - 0‖ ≤ ‖t - 0‖ := by
  simp only [sub_zero, Real.norm_eq_abs]
  rw [abs_of_nonneg (le_max_left 0 (min 1 t))]
  exact max_le (abs_nonneg t) ((min_le_right 1 t).trans (le_abs_self t))

private theorem clip_norm_sub_one (t : ℝ) :
    ‖max 0 (min 1 t) - 1‖ ≤ ‖t - 1‖ := by
  by_cases ht : t ≤ 1
  · rw [min_eq_right ht]
    have htop : max 0 t ≤ 1 := max_le zero_le_one ht
    simp only [Real.norm_eq_abs]
    rw [abs_of_nonpos (sub_nonpos.mpr htop), abs_of_nonpos (sub_nonpos.mpr ht)]
    exact neg_le_neg (sub_le_sub_right (le_max_right 0 t) 1)
  · have h1 : 1 ≤ t := (lt_of_not_ge ht).le
    rw [min_eq_left h1, max_eq_right zero_le_one, sub_self, norm_zero]
    exact norm_nonneg _

/-- For every actual measurable set, bounded continuous[0,1] functions
approximate its indicator in the original L2 seminorm to any positive tolerance. -/
theorem exists_continuous_indicator_eLpNorm_le
    (μ : Measure X) [μ.WeaklyRegular] [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : ε ≠ 0) :
    ∃ f : C(X, ℝ), (∀ x : X, 0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ 1) ∧
      eLpNorm (fun x => f x - s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x) 2 μ ≤ ε := by
  have hI : MemLp (s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))) 2 μ :=
    MemLp.indicator hs.nullMeasurableSet (memLp_const (1 : ℝ))
  obtain ⟨g, hg, _hgMemLp⟩ := hI.exists_boundedContinuous_eLpNorm_sub_le
    (by simp : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ ∞) hε
  let f : C(X, ℝ) :=
    ⟨fun x => max 0 (min 1 (g x)), continuous_const.max (continuous_const.min g.continuous)⟩
  have hf : ∀ x : X, 0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ 1 := by
    intro x
    exact ⟨le_max_left 0 (min 1 (g x)), max_le zero_le_one (min_le_left 1 (g x))⟩
  have hpoint : ∀ x : X,
      ‖f x - s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x‖ ≤
        ‖(s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) - (g : X → ℝ)) x‖ := by
    intro x
    by_cases hx : x ∈ s
    · simp only [Pi.sub_apply, indicator_of_mem hx]
      change ‖max 0 (min 1 (g x)) - 1‖ ≤ ‖1 - g x‖
      rw [norm_sub_rev (1 : ℝ) (g x)]
      exact clip_norm_sub_one (g x)
    · simp only [Pi.sub_apply, indicator_of_notMem hx]
      change ‖max 0 (min 1 (g x)) - 0‖ ≤ ‖0 - g x‖
      rw [norm_sub_rev (0 : ℝ) (g x)]
      exact clip_norm_sub_zero (g x)
  have hmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable
      (fun x => f x - s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x) μ :=
    f.continuous.aestronglyMeasurable.sub hI.aestronglyMeasurable
  exact ⟨f, hf, (eLpNorm_mono hmeas hpoint).trans hg⟩

/-- A genuine sequence of continuous[0,1] functions converges to the
measurable indicator in L2 for the same original finite measure. -/
theorem exists_continuous_indicator_l2
    (μ : Measure X) [μ.WeaklyRegular] [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    ∃ f : ℕ → C(X, ℝ), (∀ n x, 0 ≤ f n x ∧ f n x ≤ 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => f n x - s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x) 2 μ)
        atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  classical
  have happ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      ∃ f : C(X, ℝ), (∀ x : X, 0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ 1) ∧
        eLpNorm (fun x => f x - s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x) 2 μ ≤
          ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ := by
    intro n
    exact exists_continuous_indicator_eLpNorm_le μ s hs
      (ENNReal.inv_ne_zero.2 (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top (n + 1)))
  let f : ℕ → C(X, ℝ) := fun n => Classical.choose (happ n)
  have hf : ∀ n x, 0 ≤ f n x ∧ f n x ≤ 1 := fun n => (Classical.choose_spec (happ n)).1
  have herror : ∀ n : ℕ,
      eLpNorm (fun x => f n x - s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x) 2 μ ≤
        ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ := fun n => (Classical.choose_spec (happ n)).2
  have hε : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
    ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero.comp (tendsto_add_atTop_nat 1)
  refine ⟨f, hf, ?_⟩
  exact tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le tendsto_const_nhds hε
    (fun _ => bot_le) herror

/-- The same bounded continuous indicator approximation can retain both
original L2 convergence and almost-everywhere pointwise convergence. -/
theorem exists_continuous_indicator_l2_ae
    (μ : Measure X) [μ.WeaklyRegular] [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    ∃ f : ℕ → C(X, ℝ), (∀ n x, 0 ≤ f n x ∧ f n x ≤ 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (fun x => f n x - s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x) 2 μ)
        atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => f n x) atTop (𝓝 (s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x)) := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hL2⟩ := exists_continuous_indicator_l2 μ s hs
  have hmeasure : TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n x => f n x) atTop
      (s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))) :=
    tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_eLpNorm (by simp : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0) hL2
  obtain ⟨ns, hns, hae⟩ := hmeasure.exists_seq_tendsto_ae
  refine ⟨fun n => f (ns n), fun n x => hf (ns n) x, ?_, hae⟩
  exact hL2.comp hns.tendsto_atTop

end MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function

module

public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.Holder
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space

/-!
# Factoring complex `L¹` functions through `L²`

Every complex `L¹` function is the pointwise product of an `L²` function and the conjugate of
another `L²` function. The result is stated on canonical `Lp` carriers and requires no assumption on
the measure.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal ComplexConjugate MeasureTheory

namespace MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function

noncomputable section

universe u

variable {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] {mu : Measure X}

/-- Every complex `L¹` function factors as `g * conj h` for two `L²` functions. -/
theorem exists_l2_mul_star_eq (f : Lp ℂ 1 mu) :
    ∃ g h : Lp ℂ 2 mu, (g • star h : Lp ℂ 1 mu) = f := by
  let r : X → ℝ := fun x ↦ Real.sqrt ‖f x‖
  let g₀ : X → ℂ := fun x ↦ f x / (r x : ℂ)
  let h₀ : X → ℂ := fun x ↦ (r x : ℂ)
  have hg₀meas : AEStronglyMeasurable g₀ mu := by
    dsimp only [g₀, r]
    have hfmeas : AEMeasurable (fun x ↦ f x) mu := (Lp.aestronglyMeasurable f).aemeasurable
    have hrmeas : AEMeasurable (fun x ↦ (Real.sqrt ‖f x‖ : ℂ)) mu :=
      hfmeas.norm.sqrt.complex_ofReal
    exact (hfmeas.div hrmeas).aestronglyMeasurable.congr
      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun _ ↦ rfl)
  have hh₀meas : AEStronglyMeasurable h₀ mu := by
    dsimp only [h₀, r]
    fun_prop
  have hg₀norm (x : X) : ‖g₀ x‖ ^ 2 = ‖f x‖ := by
    dsimp only [g₀, r]
    rw [norm_div, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _), Real.div_sqrt,
      Real.sq_sqrt (norm_nonneg _)]
  have hh₀norm (x : X) : ‖h₀ x‖ ^ 2 = ‖f x‖ := by
    dsimp only [h₀, r]
    rw [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _),
      Real.sq_sqrt (norm_nonneg _)]
  have hfint : Integrable (fun x ↦ ‖f x‖) mu :=
    (memLp_one_iff_integrable.mp (Lp.memLp f)).norm
  have hg₀mem : MemLp g₀ 2 mu := by
    rw [memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm hg₀meas]
    simpa only [hg₀norm] using hfint
  have hh₀mem : MemLp h₀ 2 mu := by
    rw [memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm hh₀meas]
    simpa only [hh₀norm] using hfint
  let g : Lp ℂ 2 mu := hg₀mem.toLp g₀
  let h : Lp ℂ 2 mu := hh₀mem.toLp h₀
  refine ⟨g, h, ?_⟩
  apply Lp.ext
  filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_lpSMul (r := 1) g (star h), Lp.coeFn_star h,
    hg₀mem.coeFn_toLp, hh₀mem.coeFn_toLp] with x hmul hstar hg hh
  have hg' : g x = g₀ x := by simpa only [g] using hg
  have hh' : h x = h₀ x := by simpa only [h] using hh
  rw [hmul, Pi.smul_apply', hstar, Pi.star_apply, hg', hh']
  change g₀ x * star (h₀ x) = f x
  by_cases hfx : f x = 0
  · simp [g₀, h₀, r, hfx]
  · have hr : r x ≠ 0 := by
      dsimp only [r]
      exact (Real.sqrt_pos.2 (norm_pos_iff.mpr hfx)).ne'
    dsimp only [g₀, h₀]
    rw [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_ofReal, div_mul_cancel₀]
    exact_mod_cast hr

end

end MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function

module

public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.ContinuousFunctions
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.CompareExp
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.Holder
public import Mathlib.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousLinearMap
public import Mathlib.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousMap
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# Actual bounded continuous multiplication on the canonical L2 space

A bounded continuous complex function multiplies the original Lp ℂ2 μ
classes pointwise. Its actual L∞ membership and Hölder product prove L2
membership; the original pointwise bound gives the actual operator norm
bound. The original algebra and inner-product integral identities construct
the literal multiplication star representation.

This DATA is required by the original pointwise commutative representation
and normal multiplication-sum statements. The original measure is arbitrary:
no finite/probability, chosen L2 model, norm, measurability or operator
certificate is added. Empty spaces and zero measures retain their actual
canonical carriers and operators.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped ENNReal InnerProductSpace

namespace BoundedContinuousFunction

universe uX

variable {X : Type uX} [MeasurableSpace X] [TopologicalSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
variable (μ : Measure X)

/-- The original bounded function acts through the stock Hölder multiplication operator. -/
def l2MultiplicationOperator (f : X →ᵇ ℂ) : Lp ℂ 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ :=
  (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℂ ℂ).holderL μ ∞ 2 2
    ((f.memLp_top (μ := μ)).toLp f)

/-- Literal multiplication of the original L2 coefficient class by the given bounded function. -/
def mulOnL2 (f : X →ᵇ ℂ) (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) : Lp ℂ 2 μ :=
  l2MultiplicationOperator μ f u

/-- The actual result has the original pointwise product representative almost everywhere. -/
theorem mulOnL2_ae_eq (f : X →ᵇ ℂ) (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    mulOnL2 μ f u =ᵐ[μ] fun x => f x * u x := by
  have hop := (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℂ ℂ).coeFn_holder (r := 2)
    ((f.memLp_top (μ := μ)).toLp f) u
  have hf := (MemLp.coeFn_toLp (f.memLp_top (μ := μ)))
  filter_upwards [hop, hf] with x hx hfx
  change mulOnL2 μ f u x = f x * u x
  change mulOnL2 μ f u x = _ at hx
  simpa only [ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul_apply, smul_eq_mul, hfx] using hx

/-- The actual pointwise multiplication map inherits the stock operator's complex linearity. -/
def mulOnL2LinearMap (f : X →ᵇ ℂ) : Lp ℂ 2 μ →ₗ[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ :=
  (l2MultiplicationOperator μ f).toLinearMap

/-- The actual L2product is bounded by the original coefficient supremum norm and vector norm. -/
theorem mulOnL2_norm_le (f : X →ᵇ ℂ) (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    ‖mulOnL2 μ f u‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * ‖u‖ := by
  apply Lp.norm_le_mul_norm_of_ae_le_mul
  filter_upwards [mulOnL2_ae_eq μ f u] with x hx
  rw [hx, norm_mul]
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (f.norm_coe_le_norm x) (norm_nonneg (u x))

/-- The bounded multiplication operator retains the original pointwise product values almost everywhere. -/
theorem l2MultiplicationOperator_ae_eq (f : X →ᵇ ℂ) (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    l2MultiplicationOperator μ f u =ᵐ[μ] fun x => f x * u x := mulOnL2_ae_eq μ f u

/-- The actual pointwise operator norm is bounded by the original given function's sup norm. -/
theorem norm_l2MultiplicationOperator_le (f : X →ᵇ ℂ) :
    ‖l2MultiplicationOperator μ f‖ ≤ ‖f‖ :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ (norm_nonneg f) (mulOnL2_norm_le μ f)

/-- The literal pointwise multiplication representation on the original canonical L2 carrier. -/
def l2MultiplicationRepresentation : (X →ᵇ ℂ) →⋆ₐ[ℂ] (Lp ℂ 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ) where
  toFun := l2MultiplicationOperator μ
  map_one' := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro u
    change mulOnL2 μ 1 u = u
    apply Lp.ext
    filter_upwards [mulOnL2_ae_eq μ 1 u] with x hx
    simpa using hx
  map_mul' f g := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro u
    change mulOnL2 μ (f * g) u = mulOnL2 μ f (mulOnL2 μ g u)
    apply Lp.ext
    filter_upwards [mulOnL2_ae_eq μ (f * g) u, mulOnL2_ae_eq μ f (mulOnL2 μ g u),
      mulOnL2_ae_eq μ g u] with x hfg hf hg
    rw [hfg, hf, hg]
    exact mul_assoc _ _ _
  map_zero' := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro u
    change mulOnL2 μ 0 u = 0
    apply Lp.ext
    filter_upwards [mulOnL2_ae_eq μ 0 u, (Lp.coeFn_zero (E := ℂ) (p := 2) (μ := μ))] with x hx hz
    rw [hx, hz]
    simp
  map_add' f g := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro u
    change mulOnL2 μ (f + g) u = mulOnL2 μ f u + mulOnL2 μ g u
    apply Lp.ext
    filter_upwards [mulOnL2_ae_eq μ (f + g) u,
      Lp.coeFn_add (mulOnL2 μ f u) (mulOnL2 μ g u),
      mulOnL2_ae_eq μ f u, mulOnL2_ae_eq μ g u] with x hfg hsum hf hg
    rw [hfg, hsum]
    change (f x + g x) * u x = mulOnL2 μ f u x + mulOnL2 μ g u x
    rw [hf, hg]
    exact add_mul _ _ _
  commutes' c := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro u
    change mulOnL2 μ (algebraMap ℂ (X →ᵇ ℂ) c) u = c • u
    apply Lp.ext
    filter_upwards [mulOnL2_ae_eq μ (algebraMap ℂ (X →ᵇ ℂ) c) u,
      Lp.coeFn_smul c u] with x hc hu
    exact hc.trans hu.symm
  map_star' f := by
    show l2MultiplicationOperator μ (star f) = star (l2MultiplicationOperator μ f)
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.star_eq_adjoint]
    refine (ContinuousLinearMap.eq_adjoint_iff _ _).mpr ?_
    intro u v
    simp only [L2.inner_def]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [l2MultiplicationOperator_ae_eq μ (star f) u,
      l2MultiplicationOperator_ae_eq μ f v] with x hfu hfv
    rw [hfu, hfv]
    rw [RCLike.inner_apply', RCLike.inner_apply']
    simp only [← RCLike.star_def, BoundedContinuousFunction.star_apply,
      star_mul, star_star, mul_assoc]

/-- The multiplication representation keeps the literal original product representative. -/
theorem l2MultiplicationRepresentation_ae_eq (f : X →ᵇ ℂ) (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    l2MultiplicationRepresentation μ f u =ᵐ[μ] fun x => f x * u x :=
  l2MultiplicationOperator_ae_eq μ f u

end BoundedContinuousFunction

namespace ContinuousMap

universe uX

section CompactToBounded

variable {X : Type uX} [TopologicalSpace X] [CompactSpace X]

/-- Original compact-space continuous functions have their same canonical bounded star-algebra values. -/
def toBoundedStarAlgHom : C(X, ℂ) →⋆ₐ[ℂ] BoundedContinuousFunction X ℂ where
  toFun := BoundedContinuousFunction.mkOfCompact
  map_one' := rfl
  map_mul' _f _g := rfl
  map_zero' := rfl
  map_add' _f _g := rfl
  commutes' _c := rfl
  map_star' _f := rfl

end CompactToBounded

variable {X : Type uX} [MeasurableSpace X] [TopologicalSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompactSpace X]

/-- The actual continuous-function multiplication representation on the original arbitrary-measure L2space. -/
def l2MultiplicationRepresentation (μ : Measure X) :
    C(X, ℂ) →⋆ₐ[ℂ] (Lp ℂ 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ) :=
  (BoundedContinuousFunction.l2MultiplicationRepresentation μ).comp toBoundedStarAlgHom

/-- Every original continuous coefficient keeps its literal original L2product values almost everywhere. -/
theorem l2MultiplicationRepresentation_ae_eq (μ : Measure X) (f : C(X, ℂ)) (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    l2MultiplicationRepresentation μ f u =ᵐ[μ] fun x => f x * u x :=
  BoundedContinuousFunction.l2MultiplicationRepresentation_ae_eq μ
    (BoundedContinuousFunction.mkOfCompact f) u

end ContinuousMap

end

module

public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space.TensorProduct

/-!
# The actual H-first scalar L2 Hilbert tensor

The stock tensor commutation isometry and its inverse extend through the
literal completions. Composing with the computed scalar-first comparison
gives the original H-first tensor its exact vector-valued L2 coordinates.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Filter
open scoped TensorProduct ENNReal InnerProductSpace

namespace MeasureTheory.L2

noncomputable section

universe uX uH uK

variable {X : Type uX} [MeasurableSpace X]
variable {𝕜 : Type uK} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {H : Type uH} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H] [CompleteSpace H]
variable (μ : Measure X)

/-- The original H-first completed scalar L2 tensor has its actual vector L2 coordinates. -/
def tensorToLpRight : UniformSpace.Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] Lp H 2 μ := by
  let c := TensorProduct.commIsometry 𝕜 H (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)
  let f := c.toLinearIsometry.completion
  let g := c.symm.toLinearIsometry.completion
  have hfg : f.toLinearMap.comp g.toLinearMap = LinearMap.id := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro z
    change f (g z) = z
    refine UniformSpace.Completion.induction_on z
      (isClosed_eq (f.continuous.comp g.continuous) continuous_id) ?_
    intro z
    change c.toLinearIsometry.completion
        (c.symm.toLinearIsometry.completion
          (z : UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H))) =
      (z : UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H))
    rw [LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe, LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe]
    exact congrArg (fun z : (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H =>
      (z : UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H))) (c.apply_symm_apply z)
  have hgf : g.toLinearMap.comp f.toLinearMap = LinearMap.id := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro z
    change g (f z) = z
    refine UniformSpace.Completion.induction_on z
      (isClosed_eq (g.continuous.comp f.continuous) continuous_id) ?_
    intro z
    change c.symm.toLinearIsometry.completion
        (c.toLinearIsometry.completion
          (z : UniformSpace.Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)))) =
      (z : UniformSpace.Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)))
    rw [LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe, LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe]
    exact congrArg (fun z : H ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) =>
      (z : UniformSpace.Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)))) (c.symm_apply_apply z)
  let E := LinearIsometryEquiv.ofLinearIsometry f g.toLinearMap hfg hgf
  exact E.trans (tensorToLp (𝕜 := 𝕜) (H := H) μ)

/-- Each original H-first pure tensor has the exact scalar-vector formula almost everywhere. -/
theorem tensorToLpRight_tmul_ae (x : H) (f : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) :
    tensorToLpRight μ ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] f : H ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) :
        UniformSpace.Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))) =ᵐ[μ] fun s => f s • x := by
  change tensorToLp μ
      ((TensorProduct.commIsometry 𝕜 H (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)).toLinearIsometry.completion
        ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] f : H ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) :
          UniformSpace.Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)))) =ᵐ[μ] _
  rw [LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe]
  change tensorToLp μ
      ((f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] x : (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H) :
        UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H)) =ᵐ[μ] _
  exact tensorToLp_tmul_ae μ f x

end

end MeasureTheory.L2

Author: @toskua

module

public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space.RightTensorProduct
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.CompletionMap

/-!
# Actual constant operators in H-first tensor L2 coordinates

The original completed tensor map on the Hilbert factor is exactly the
existing pointwise Lp composition map in the computed L2 coordinates.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Filter
open scoped TensorProduct ENNReal Topology

namespace MeasureTheory.L2

noncomputable section

universe uX uK uH₁ uH₂

variable {X : Type uX} [MeasurableSpace X]
variable {𝕜 : Type uK} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {H₁ : Type uH₁} [NormedAddCommGroup H₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H₁] [CompleteSpace H₁]
variable {H₂ : Type uH₂} [NormedAddCommGroup H₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H₂] [CompleteSpace H₂]

/-- The original completed tensor operator has its actual pointwise vector L2 value. -/
theorem tensorToLpRight_mapLCompletion (μ : Measure X) (B : H₁ →L[𝕜] H₂)
    (z : UniformSpace.Completion (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))) :
    tensorToLpRight μ
        (TensorProduct.mapLCompletion B (ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) z) =
      B.compLpL 2 μ (tensorToLpRight μ z) := by
  let m : PseudoMetricSpace (UniformSpace.Completion (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))) :=
    (inferInstance : SeminormedAddCommGroup
      (UniformSpace.Completion (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)))).toPseudoMetricSpace
  have hUniform : m.toUniformSpace = UniformSpace.Completion.uniformSpace (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) := by
    apply UniformSpace.ext
    exact (@PseudoMetricSpace.uniformity_dist _ m).trans
      (UniformSpace.Completion.uniformity_dist (α := H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))).symm
  have htop : m.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace =
      (UniformSpace.Completion.uniformSpace (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))).toTopologicalSpace :=
    congrArg (fun w : UniformSpace (UniformSpace.Completion (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))) =>
      @UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace (UniformSpace.Completion (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))) w) hUniform
  have toStockClosed (s : Set (UniformSpace.Completion (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))))
      (hs : @IsClosed _ m.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace s) :
      @IsClosed _ (UniformSpace.Completion.uniformSpace (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))).toTopologicalSpace s := by
    rw [htop] at hs
    exact hs
  refine UniformSpace.Completion.induction_on z (toStockClosed _
    (isClosed_eq
      ((tensorToLpRight (H := H₂) μ).continuous.comp
        (TensorProduct.mapLCompletion B (ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))).continuous)
      ((B.compLpL 2 μ).continuous.comp (tensorToLpRight (H := H₁) μ).continuous))) ?_
  intro z
  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul x f =>
    rw [TensorProduct.mapLCompletion_tmul]
    change tensorToLpRight μ ((B x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] f : H₂ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) :
        UniformSpace.Completion (H₂ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))) =
      B.compLpL 2 μ (tensorToLpRight μ ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] f : H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) :
        UniformSpace.Completion (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ))))
    apply Lp.ext
    filter_upwards [tensorToLpRight_tmul_ae μ (B x) f,
      B.coeFn_compLpL (tensorToLpRight μ ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] f : H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) :
        UniformSpace.Completion (H₁ ⊗[𝕜] (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)))),
      tensorToLpRight_tmul_ae μ x f] with s hleft hmap hright
    rw [hleft, hmap, hright, map_smul]
  | add z w hz hw => simp only [UniformSpace.Completion.coe_add, map_add, hz, hw]

end

end MeasureTheory.L2

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Completion
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Extend
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Mul
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.SimpleFuncDenseLp

/-!
# The completed scalar L2 tensor is the actual Hilbert-valued L2 space

The carrier is the stock completion of the stock inner-product tensor norm.
Its comparison sends a pure tensor to pointwise scalar multiplication. The
inner-product integral proves isometry; finite-measure indicators and the
existing Lp induction theorem prove surjectivity for an arbitrary measure.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Filter
open scoped TensorProduct ENNReal InnerProductSpace

namespace MeasureTheory.L2

noncomputable section

universe uX uH uK

variable {X : Type uX} [MeasurableSpace X]
variable {𝕜 : Type uK} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {H : Type uH} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H]
variable (μ : Measure X)

/-- Pointwise scalar multiplication, computed by the existing Lp composition functor. -/
def scalarVector : Lp 𝕜 2 μ →L[𝕜] H →L[𝕜] Lp H 2 μ :=
  ((ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul 𝕜 𝕜 : 𝕜 →L[𝕜] H →L[𝕜] H).flip.compLpL₂ 2 μ).flip

/-- The actual scalar-vector Lp map has its original pointwise representative almost everywhere. -/
theorem scalarVector_ae_eq (f : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (x : H) :
    scalarVector μ f x =ᵐ[μ] fun s => f s • x := by
  change (ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 x).compLp f =ᵐ[μ] fun s => f s • x
  exact (ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 x).coeFn_compLp f

/-- The actual pointwise integral has the stock pure-tensor inner product. -/
private theorem scalarVector_inner (f g : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (x y : H) :
    inner 𝕜 (scalarVector μ f x) (scalarVector μ g y) = inner 𝕜 f g * inner 𝕜 x y := by
  change inner 𝕜 ((ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 x).compLp f)
      ((ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 y).compLp g) = inner 𝕜 f g * inner 𝕜 x y
  simp only [L2.inner_def]
  rw [← integral_mul_const]
  apply integral_congr_ae
  filter_upwards [(ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 x).coeFn_compLp f,
    (ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 y).coeFn_compLp g] with s hx hy
  rw [hx, hy, ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply]
  simp only [inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, RCLike.inner_apply', mul_assoc]
  exact mul_left_comm _ _ _

/-- The algebraic tensor lift of the computed pointwise bilinear map. -/
def tensorToLpLinearMap : (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H →ₗ[𝕜] Lp H 2 μ :=
  TensorProduct.lift (scalarVector μ).toLinearMap₁₂

/-- The actual algebraic lift sends each pure tensor to its original scalar-vector Lp value. -/
@[simp]
theorem tensorToLpLinearMap_tmul (f : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (x : H) :
    tensorToLpLinearMap μ (f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] x) = (ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 x).compLp f := by
  change TensorProduct.lift (scalarVector μ).toLinearMap₁₂ (f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] x) = _
  rw [TensorProduct.lift.tmul]
  rfl

/-- The lift preserves the actual tensor inner product, by bilinearity on pure tensors. -/
theorem tensorToLpLinearMap_inner (z w : (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H) :
    inner 𝕜 (tensorToLpLinearMap μ z) (tensorToLpLinearMap μ w) = inner 𝕜 z w := by
  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul f x =>
    induction w using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul g y =>
      change inner 𝕜 (scalarVector μ f x) (scalarVector μ g y) = inner 𝕜 f g * inner 𝕜 x y
      exact scalarVector_inner μ f g x y
    | add z w hz hw => simp only [map_add, inner_add_right, hz, hw]
  | add z w hz hw => simp only [map_add, inner_add_left, hz, hw]

variable [CompleteSpace H]

/-- The proved algebraic isometry extends to the same literal stock tensor completion. -/
def tensorToLpEmbedding :
    UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H) →ₗᵢ[𝕜] Lp H 2 μ :=
  ((tensorToLpLinearMap μ).isometryOfInner (tensorToLpLinearMap_inner μ)).fromCompletion

/-- The extension retains every algebraic tensor value. -/
theorem tensorToLpEmbedding_coe (z : (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H) :
    tensorToLpEmbedding μ (z : UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H)) =
      tensorToLpLinearMap μ z :=
  LinearIsometry.fromCompletion_apply_coe _ z

/-- The actual completed scalar L2 Hilbert tensor is canonically the actual vector-valued L2 space. -/
def tensorToLp : UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] Lp H 2 μ := by
  let I := tensorToLpEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (H := H) μ
  have hclosed : IsClosed (Set.range I) := I.isometry.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range
  have hsurj : Function.Surjective I := by
    apply Lp.induction (p := 2) (by simp) (fun f => ∃ z, I z = f)
    · intro x s hs hμs
      refine ⟨((indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs.ne (1 : 𝕜)) ⊗ₜ[𝕜] x :
        UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H)), ?_⟩
      change tensorToLpEmbedding μ
          (((indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs.ne (1 : 𝕜)) ⊗ₜ[𝕜] x) :
            UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H)) =
        (Lp.simpleFunc.indicatorConst 2 hs hμs.ne x : Lp H 2 μ)
      rw [tensorToLpEmbedding_coe]
      change (ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 x).compLp
          (indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs.ne (1 : 𝕜)) = indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs.ne x
      apply Lp.ext
      have hscalar : indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs.ne (1 : 𝕜) =ᵐ[μ]
          s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : 𝕜)) := indicatorConstLp_coeFn
      have hvector : indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs.ne x =ᵐ[μ]
          s.indicator (fun _ => x) := indicatorConstLp_coeFn
      filter_upwards [(ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 x).coeFn_compLp
        (indicatorConstLp 2 hs hμs.ne (1 : 𝕜)), hscalar, hvector] with a hmap ha hx
      rw [hmap, ha, hx, ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply]
      by_cases h : a ∈ s <;> simp [h]
    · intro _f _g _hf _hg _hdisjoint hfx hgy
      obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hfx
      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hgy
      exact ⟨x + y, by rw [map_add, hx, hy]⟩
    · exact hclosed
  exact LinearIsometryEquiv.ofSurjective I hsurj

/-- Every completed pure tensor has the exact computed scalar-vector Lp value. -/
@[simp]
theorem tensorToLp_tmul (f : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (x : H) :
    tensorToLp μ ((f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] x : (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H) :
        UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H)) =
      (ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 x).compLp f := by
  change tensorToLpEmbedding μ ((f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] x : (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H) :
    UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H)) = _
  rw [tensorToLpEmbedding_coe]
  rfl

/-- The completed pure-tensor comparison retains the original pointwise formula almost everywhere. -/
theorem tensorToLp_tmul_ae (f : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (x : H) :
    tensorToLp μ ((f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] x : (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H) :
        UniformSpace.Completion ((Lp 𝕜 2 μ) ⊗[𝕜] H)) =ᵐ[μ] fun s => f s • x := by
  rw [tensorToLp_tmul]
  exact (ContinuousLinearMap.toSpanSingleton 𝕜 x).coeFn_compLp f

end

end MeasureTheory.L2

module

public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.Basic
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Basic
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.SMul
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.TriangleInequality
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.LinearPMap
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# Actual maximal pointwise multiplication on the canonical L2classes

The original measure and complex coefficient function define the exact
submodule of Lpℂ2μ whose pointwise product belongs to L2. Every value is
the stock MemLp.toLp class of that product. The actual representative
identities construct the linear map and canonical LinearPMap domain.
No finite/probability/sigma-finite measure, bounded coefficient, selected
operator, desired norm or source theorem output is an input.

The same construction specializes to real-coordinate multiplication and
to coefficient functions used by operator calculi. Spectral, density,
closedness and self-adjointness results are separate from this constructor.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open Filter
open scoped ENNReal

namespace MeasureTheory.Lp

universe uX

variable {X : Type uX} [MeasurableSpace X]
variable (μ : Measure X) (m : X → ℂ)

/-- The actual maximal domain consists precisely of original L2classes with L2pointwise product. -/
def multiplicationDomain : Submodule ℂ (Lp ℂ 2 μ) where
  carrier := {u | MemLp (fun x => m x * u x) 2 μ}
  zero_mem' := by
    have hzero : (fun x => m x * (0 : Lp ℂ 2 μ) x) =ᵐ[μ] fun _ => (0 : ℂ) := by
      filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_zero (E := ℂ) (p := 2) (μ := μ)] with x hx
      simp only [hx, Pi.zero_apply, mul_zero]
    exact (memLp_congr_ae hzero).2 MemLp.zero'
  add_mem' := by
    intro u v hu hv
    change MemLp (fun x => m x * u x) 2 μ at hu
    change MemLp (fun x => m x * v x) 2 μ at hv
    have hsum := hu.add hv
    refine (memLp_congr_ae (show (fun x => m x * (u + v) x) =ᵐ[μ]
      (fun x => m x * u x) + (fun x => m x * v x) from ?_)).2 hsum
    filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_add u v] with x hx
    simp only [hx, Pi.add_apply, mul_add]
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c u hu
    change MemLp (fun x => m x * u x) 2 μ at hu
    have hsmul := hu.const_smul c
    refine (memLp_congr_ae (show (fun x => m x * (c • u) x) =ᵐ[μ]
      c • (fun x => m x * u x) from ?_)).2 hsmul
    filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_smul c u] with x hx
    simp only [hx, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    ring

/-- Maximal-domain membership is the exact original L2pointwise-product condition. -/
theorem mem_multiplicationDomain (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) :
    u ∈ multiplicationDomain μ m ↔ MemLp (fun x => m x * u x) 2 μ := Iff.rfl

/-- The actual product class of an original domain member, with no chosen representative or output model. -/
def multiplicationValue (u : multiplicationDomain μ m) : Lp ℂ 2 μ :=
  (u.property : MemLp (fun x => m x * (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) x) 2 μ).toLp
    (fun x => m x * (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) x)

/-- Every maximal-domain product keeps the original pointwise multiplication values almost everywhere. -/
theorem multiplicationValue_ae_eq (u : multiplicationDomain μ m) :
    multiplicationValue μ m u =ᵐ[μ] fun x => m x * (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) x :=
  MemLp.coeFn_toLp _

/-- The original pointwise representative identities give the actual complex-linear product map. -/
def multiplicationLinearMap : multiplicationDomain μ m →ₗ[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ where
  toFun := multiplicationValue μ m
  map_add' := by
    intro u v
    apply Lp.ext
    filter_upwards [multiplicationValue_ae_eq μ m (u + v),
      Lp.coeFn_add (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) (v : Lp ℂ 2 μ),
      Lp.coeFn_add (multiplicationValue μ m u) (multiplicationValue μ m v),
      multiplicationValue_ae_eq μ m u, multiplicationValue_ae_eq μ m v]
      with x huv hin hout hu hv
    rw [huv, hout]
    simp only [Submodule.coe_add]
    rw [hin]
    change m x * ((u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) x + (v : Lp ℂ 2 μ) x) =
      multiplicationValue μ m u x + multiplicationValue μ m v x
    rw [hu, hv]
    exact mul_add _ _ _
  map_smul' := by
    intro c u
    apply Lp.ext
    filter_upwards [multiplicationValue_ae_eq μ m (c • u),
      Lp.coeFn_smul c (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ), Lp.coeFn_smul c (multiplicationValue μ m u),
      multiplicationValue_ae_eq μ m u] with x hcu hin hout hu
    change multiplicationValue μ m (c • u) x = (c • multiplicationValue μ m u) x
    rw [hcu, hout]
    simp only [Submodule.coe_smul]
    rw [hin]
    simp only [Pi.smul_apply]
    rw [hu]
    simp only [smul_eq_mul]
    ring

/-- The canonical unbounded multiplication operator on the actual maximal domain. -/
def multiplicationOperator : Lp ℂ 2 μ →ₗ.[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 μ :=
  LinearPMap.mk (multiplicationDomain μ m) (multiplicationLinearMap μ m)

/-- The actual unbounded operator has precisely the original maximal product domain. -/
theorem multiplicationOperator_domain :
    (multiplicationOperator μ m).domain = multiplicationDomain μ m := rfl

/-- The canonical partial operator keeps every original pointwise product representative. -/
theorem multiplicationOperator_ae_eq (u : (multiplicationOperator μ m).domain) :
    multiplicationOperator μ m u =ᵐ[μ] fun x => m x * (u : Lp ℂ 2 μ) x :=
  multiplicationValue_ae_eq μ m u

end MeasureTheory.Lp

end

module

public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Set
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.ClosedSubmodule

/-!
# Closed subspaces of Lp supported on a measurable set

The carrier is the literal almost everywhere vanishing condition off the
set. Closedness follows from the kernel of the actual restriction map to
its complement. No completeness or finite-measure hypothesis is needed.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section
open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ENNReal
namespace MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function

universe u v w
variable {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X]
variable {𝕜 : Type v} [NormedField 𝕜]
variable {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {p : ℝ≥0∞} [Fact (1 ≤ p)]

/-- The actual Lp subspace of functions that vanish almost everywhere off a set. -/
def Lp.supportedOn (mu : Measure X) (s : Set X) : Submodule 𝕜 (Lp E p mu) where
  carrier := {f | ∀ᵐ x ∂mu, x ∉ s → f x = 0}
  zero_mem' := by
    filter_upwards [MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_zero E p mu] with x hx
    intro _
    exact hx
  add_mem' := by
    intro f g hf hg
    filter_upwards [hf, hg, MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_add f g] with x hfx hgx hadd
    intro hx
    exact hadd.trans (by rw [Pi.add_apply, hfx hx, hgx hx, add_zero])
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c f hf
    filter_upwards [hf, MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_smul c f] with x hfx hsmul
    intro hx
    exact hsmul.trans (by rw [Pi.smul_apply, hfx hx, smul_zero])

omit [Fact (1 ≤ p)] in
/-- The defining support condition retains the original ambient almost everywhere measure.
This equivalence holds for every exponent `p : ℝ≥0∞`. -/
theorem Lp.mem_supportedOn (mu : Measure X) (s : Set X) (f : Lp E p mu) :
    f ∈ Lp.supportedOn (𝕜 := 𝕜) mu s ↔ ∀ᵐ x ∂mu, x ∉ s → f x = 0 := Iff.rfl

/-- Almost everywhere support is exactly zero under the actual complement restriction map. -/
theorem Lp.supportedOn_eq_ker_restrict (mu : Measure X) (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    Lp.supportedOn (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (p := p) mu s =
      (LpToLpRestrictCLM X E 𝕜 mu p sᶜ).ker := by
  apply Submodule.ext
  intro f
  change (∀ᵐ x ∂mu, x ∉ s → f x = 0) ↔ LpToLpRestrictCLM X E 𝕜 mu p sᶜ f = 0
  rw [MeasureTheory.Lp.eq_zero_iff_ae_eq_zero]
  have hrep := LpToLpRestrictCLM_coeFn 𝕜 sᶜ f
  constructor
  · intro hf
    have hf' : f =ᵐ[mu.restrict sᶜ] 0 := (ae_restrict_iff' hs.compl).2 hf
    exact hrep.trans hf'
  · intro hf
    have hf' : f =ᵐ[mu.restrict sᶜ] 0 := hrep.symm.trans hf
    exact (ae_restrict_iff' hs.compl).1 hf'

/-- Support on a measurable set is a closed Lp subspace, proved by its actual restriction kernel. -/
theorem Lp.isClosed_supportedOn (mu : Measure X) (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    IsClosed (Lp.supportedOn (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (p := p) mu s : Set (Lp E p mu)) := by
  rw [Lp.supportedOn_eq_ker_restrict mu s hs]
  exact (LpToLpRestrictCLM X E 𝕜 mu p sᶜ).isClosed_ker

/-- The actual closed support subspace, with the literal almost everywhere carrier. -/
def Lp.closedSupportedOn (mu : Measure X) (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    ClosedSubmodule 𝕜 (Lp E p mu) :=
  ⟨Lp.supportedOn mu s, Lp.isClosed_supportedOn mu s hs⟩

/-- Values of the closed support space still satisfy the original vanishing condition. -/
theorem Lp.mem_closedSupportedOn (mu : Measure X) (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    (f : Lp E p mu) :
    f ∈ Lp.closedSupportedOn (𝕜 := 𝕜) mu s hs ↔ ∀ᵐ x ∂mu, x ∉ s → f x = 0 := Iff.rfl

end MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function
